[[ja:%E5%8C%97%E9%87%8E%E5%A4%A9%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE_(%E6%89%80%E6%B2%A2%E5%B8%82)]] [[Category:11]][[sn:Kitano Tenjinja (Tokorozawa)]][[Category:11]] [[Category:11]][[sn:Kitano Tenjinja (Tokorozawa)]][[Category:11]] [[Category:11]][[sn:Kitano Tenjinja (Tokorozawa)]][[Category:11]] [[Category:11]][[sn:Kitano Tenjinja (Tokorozawa)]][[Category:11]] [[Category:11]][[sn:Kitano Tenjinja (Tokorozawa)]][[Category:11]] [[Category:11]][[sn:Kitano Tenjinja (Tokorozawa)]][[Category:11]]{{citation needed|Kitano Tenjinja (Tokorozawa)}}[[Category:11]] [[Category:11]]{{DEFAULTSORT:Kitano Tenjinja (Tokorozawa)}}[[Category:11]] [[Category:Kitano Tenjinja (Tokorozawa)]][[Category:Kitano Tenjinja (Tokorozawa)]] [[Category:11]][[ceb:Kitano Tenjinja (Tokorozawa)]][[Category:11]] [[sn:Kitano Tenjinja (Tokorozawa)]][[Category:11]][[sn:Kitano Tenjinja (Tokorozawa)]][[Category:11]][[sn:Kitano Tenjinja (Tokorozawa)]][[Category:11]][[sn:Kitano Tenjinja (Tokorozawa)]][[Category:11]][[sn:Kitano Tenjinja (Tokorozawa)]][[Category:11]] [[Category:11]][[sn:Kitano Tenjinja (Tokorozawa)]][[Category:11]] '''Kitano Tenjinsha''' (北野天神社) == Location == * Address: 3-28-44 Kotesashi Motomachi, Tokorozawa City, Saitama Prefecture, Japan * Coordinates: 35°47'26.0"N, 139°25'43.3"E == Enshrined Deities == * '''Mononobe Tenjinsha (物部天神社):''' Kushitama Nigihayahi no Mikoto (櫛玉饒速日命) * '''Kuniichigi Jinja (国渭地祇神社):''' Yachihoko no Mikoto (八千矛命) * '''Tenman Tenjinsha (天満天神社):''' Sugawara no Michizane (Sugawara no Michizane) === Additional Deities === * Prince Muneyoshi (宗良親王) * Kotesashi Myojin (小手指明神) * Amenohohi no Mikoto (天穂日命) * Emperor Ojin (応神天皇) * Yamato Takeru no Mikoto (日本武尊命) * Ukanomitama no Mikoto (倉稲魂命) == History == The shrine's origins are attributed to Yamato Takeru during his Eastern expedition. The Mononobe Tenjinsha served as the ancestral shrine for the Mononobe clan. The Tenjinsha was established in 995 AD by Sugawara no Shusei, a descendant of Sugawara no Michizane, who enshrined the deity from Kitano Shrine in Kyoto. The shrine received official recognition from the Tokugawa Shogunate and saw contributions from historical figures such as Minamoto no Yoshiie, Minamoto no Yoritomo, Ashikaga Takauji, and Maeda Toshiie. == Festivals and Rituals == * '''New Year's Festival (January 1)''' * '''Setsubun Festival (February 3)''' * '''Hatsuuma Festival (February 11)''' * '''Kinensai (February 27)''' * '''Spring Grand Festival (March 21)''' * '''Spring Festival (March 25)''' * '''Silkworm Festival (April 3)''' * '''Memorial Service (April 15)''' * '''Yakumo Festival (July 14-15)''' * '''Autumn Grand Festival (Late September)''' * '''Niinamesai (November 23)''' == Cultural Properties == * '''Saitama Prefecture Designated Cultural Property:''' Kitano Tenjin Engi (painted scroll) * '''Tokorozawa City Designated Cultural Property:''' ** Song Monument of Mikoto Sakura ** Medieval documents related to Kitano Tenjinsha == Associated Shrines == * Fujimori Inari Jinja * Rokusho Jinja * Suwa Jinja == Notable Features == * Mikoto Sakura (Sacred Cherry Tree) * Dainagon Plum Tree (planted by Maeda Toshiie) * Ayako Tenjinsha (dedicated to Sugawara no Michizane's wet nurse) * Aviation Shrine (relocated from the former Tokorozawa Army Airfield) == Access Information == Kitano Tenjinsha is accessible from Kotesashi Station with a short walk. == External Links == * [Official Website](https://kitanotenjin.com/) * [Saitama Shrine Association](https://www.saitama-jinjacho.or.jp/shrine/8910/) {{神社 |名称 = {{ill|Mononobe Tenjinsha|ja|物部天神社}}・{{ill|Kuniichi Jigishinja|ja|国渭地祇神社}}
・{{ill|Tenmantenjinja|ja|天満天神社}} |image = [[File:Kitanoten-jinja (Tokorozawa), haiden.jpg|250px]]
拝殿 |所在地 = {{ill|Saitama Prefecture|ja|埼玉県}}{{ill|Tokorozawa City|ja|所沢市}}{{ill|Kotesashi Motomachi|ja|小手指元町}}3-28-44 |位置 = {{Coord|35|47|26.0|N|139|25|43.3|E|region:JP-11_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name={{ill|Kitano Tenjin Shrine|ja|北野天神社}}}} |祭神 = {{ill|Nigihayahi|ja|ニギハヤヒ|lt=Kushitama Nigi Hayahito|lt_ja=櫛玉饒速日命}}
{{ill|Okunitama|ja|大国主|lt=Yachihoko no Mikoto|lt_ja=八千矛命}}
{{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|ja|Sugawara no Michizane}} |社格 = {{ill|Engishiki Shinmeichō|ja|延喜式神名帳|lt=Shikinaisha|lt_ja=式内社}}（小2・小1{{ill|Ronsha|ja|論社}}）
{{ill|Kensha|ja|県社}} |創建 = 不明 |本殿 = |別名 = 北野天神社（総称） |例祭 = {{ill|March 21|ja|3月21日}}（春の例大祭） |神事 = |地図 = {{Location map|Japan Saitama|label={{ill|Kitano Tenjin Shrine|ja|北野天神社}}|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20|float=center|border=none|position=top|width=210|caption=}} {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=12|frame-align=center|frame-width=210}} }} [[File:Kitano-Tenjin-sha sandō.jpg|thumb|北野天神社 南側参道にて]] '''Kitano Tenjin Shrine''' (北野天神社, きたのてんじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto Shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Saitama Prefecture|ja|埼玉県}}, {{ill|Tokorozawa City|ja|所沢市}}, {{ill|Kotesashi Motomachi|ja|小手指元町}}. It is classified as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} (two subsidiary shrines of the smaller class and one of the larger class according to the system of the {{ill|Engishiki Shinmeichō|ja|延喜式神名帳}}), with its former ranking under the modern shrine ranking system being that of a {{ill|Kensha|ja|県社}}. The registered name of the religious corporation is '''{{ill|Mononobe Tenjinsha|ja|物部天神社}}・{{ill|Kuniichi Jigishinja|ja|國渭地祇神社}}・{{ill|Tenmantenjinja|ja|天満天神社}}'''; "Kitano Tenjin Shrine" is a collective term for these shrines.{{Cite web|and=|url=http://www.city.tokorozawa.saitama.jp/iitokoro/enjoy/kids/shokai/meisyokyuseki/kitanotenjinsya.html |title=北野天神社（きたのてんじんしゃ）（北野） |date=2008-10-31 |publisher=Tokorozawa City Education Committee, Cultural Property Protection Division |accessdate=2015-06}} == 祭神 == * {{ill|Mononobe Tenjinsha|ja|物部天神社}} (もののべてんじんじゃ): Enshrines {{ill|Nigihayahi|ja|ニギハヤヒ|lt=Kushitama Nigi Hayahito|lt_ja=饒速日命}}, designated as the subsidiary shrine "Mononobe Tenjinsha" within the system; it is enshrined together with {{ill|Izumo Ihabishi Shrine|ja|出雲伊波比神社}}. * {{ill|Kuniichi Jigishinja|ja|国渭地祇神社}} (くにいちぎじんじゃ): Enshrines {{ill|Okunitama|ja|大国主|lt=Yachihoko no Mikoto|lt_ja=八千矛命}}, designated as the subsidiary shrine "Kuniichi Jigisha" ({{ill|Izumo Ihabishi Shrine|ja|出雲伊波比神社}} is enshrined together). * {{ill|Tenmantenjinja|ja|天満天神社}} (てんまんてんじんじゃ): Enshrines {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|ja|Sugawara no Michizane}}. === 合祀 === * {{ill|Souryo Prince|ja|宗良親王}} (むねよししんのう) * {{ill|Kotesashi Myojin|ja|小手指明神}} * {{ill|Ameno Hohi|ja|アメノホヒ|lt=Amenohohi no Mikoto|lt_ja=天穂日命}} * {{ill|Oujin Tennō|ja|応神天皇|lt=Emperor Ojin|lt_ja=應神天皇}} * {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|ヤマトタケル|lt=Prince Yamato Takeru|lt_ja=日本武尊命}} * {{ill|Ukano Mitama|ja|ウカノミタマ|lt=Ukano Mitama no Mikoto|lt_ja=倉稲魂命}} == History == According to shrine tradition, it is said that {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|日本武尊|1=Yamato Takeru|lt=Prince Yamato Takeru|3=ヤマトタケル}} enshrined this site during his eastern expedition. In the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, the Edo Bakufu granted {{ill|Shuinjo|ja|朱印状}} to the shrine. * The Mononobe Tenjinsha was the tutelary shrine of the Mononobe clan (see {{ill|Mujashi Kunizukuri|ja|无邪志国造}} for the family) and continues to enshrine their ancestral deity, {{ill|Nigihayahi|ja|ニギハヤヒ}}. * As a Tenjin Shrine, it was first enshrined by {{ill|Sugawara no Shūsei|ja|菅原修成}}, a 5th-generation descendant of {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|ja|Sugawara no Michizane}}, in the first year of the {{ill|Chōtoku|ja|長徳}} era (995) as a guardian in his capacity as {{ill|Musashi-no-Mori|ja|武蔵守}}, sent from Kyoto's {{ill|Kitano Tenmangu|ja|北野天満宮|lt=Kitano Shrine|lt_ja=北野神社}}. Subsequently, the shrine buildings were constructed under the auspices of figures such as {{ill|Minamoto no Yoshiie|ja|源義家}}, {{ill|Minamoto no Yoritomo|ja|源頼朝}}, {{ill|Ashikaga Takauji|ja|足利尊氏}}, and {{ill|Maeda Toshiie|ja|前田利家}}. * Edo Shukkai-chō – From April 1 to 6 in the 7th year of the {{ill|Kyōhō|ja|享保}} era (1722), an opening ceremony ({{ill|Shukkai-chō|ja|出開帳}}) for the shrine's sacred object was held at the former {{ill|Mejiro Fudōin Hasedera|ja|目白不動院長谷寺}} in Edo, and on April 24 during that period, temple treasures such as hanging scrolls and documents were submitted to Edo Castle at the behest of the shogun.{{Cite web|和書|url=https://www.asahi-net.or.jp/~hm9k-ajm/musasinorekisi/gosikifudoutomusasino/mejirofudou/kitanotennjinndekaityou/kitanotennjinnsyadekaityou.htm |title=北野天神社江戸出開帳 |work=おたまじゃくし |date=2001-11-11 |publisher=Yasushima Kiichi|accessdate=2015-06}} == Shrine Grounds == Within the shrine precincts, a sanmichi (approach path) lined with {{ill|torii|ja|鳥居}} and {{ill|stone lanterns|ja|石灯籠}} is located on the west and south sides. The west side faces the old {{ill|Kamakura Kaidō|ja|鎌倉街道}}, which runs north–south, and from the south side along {{ill|Saitama-Tokyo Road 179|ja|県道179号線}}, multiple staircases and torii lead up to the haiden (worship hall). ; Shrines Within the Grounds * {{ill|Inari Shrine|ja|稲荷社}} * {{ill|Yakumo Shrine|ja|八雲社}} * {{ill|Kōkūjinja (Tokorozawa)|ja|航空神社}} – Established on September 25, Showa 12 by {{ill|Tokugawa Yoshitoshi|ja|徳川好敏}}, at the {{ill|Tokorozawa Army Airfield|ja|所沢陸軍飛行場}}. Its establishment was inspired by the plight of aviation personnel who sacrificed their lives for the development of national aviation yet were not enshrined at {{ill|Yasukuni Shrine|ja|靖国神社}}; it was thus determined that a guardian deity for national aviation should be enshrined. In Showa 13, with the founding of the {{ill|Army Air Officer Academy|ja|陸軍航空士官学校}}, the shrine was relocated from Tokorozawa to Toyooka (present-day {{ill|Iruma Base|ja|入間基地}}). On September 3, Showa 20, before the academy site was seized by the U.S. military, the shrine was re-situated within its present grounds. * {{ill|Fumiko Tenjin Shrine|ja|文子天神社}} – Enshrines Fumiko, who served as the wet nurse ({{ill|wet nurse|ja|乳母}}) of {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|ja|Sugawara no Michizane}}, known as {{ill|Tajihi Fumiko|ja|多治比文子}}. * {{ill|Kotesashi Jinja|ja|小手指神社}} – Enshrines the war dead (heroic spirits) of the Kotesashi area. ; Trees on the Grounds * {{ill|Mikotozakura|ja|尊桜}} – A cherry tree said to have been planted in front of the shrine by {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|ヤマトタケル}}, which repeatedly dies and regrows (exhibiting {{ill|Noda|ja|蘖（ひこばえ）}}). * {{ill|Dainagon Ume|ja|大納言梅}} – Planted in the 18th year of the {{ill|Tenshō Era|ja|天正}} (1590) by {{ill|Maeda Toshiie|ja|前田利家}}, currently the second generation as of 2015. It is said that Maeda Toshiie, who claimed descent from {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|ja|Sugawara no Michizane}} and used the Ume crest ({{ill|Ume Crest|ja|梅紋}}), revived the shrine by planting a single plum tree during the 【ill|Odawara Campaign|ja|小田原攻め】; his title at that time was {{ill|Dainagon|ja|大納言}}. ; Other Elements Within the Grounds * A stone monument recording the origin of the local name "Kitano" – Established on September 25, {{ill|Heisei|ja|平成}} 18 (2006). Although recent land reorganization has changed the shrine's address to Kotesashi Motomachi, the surrounding area retains the name "Kitano" as derived from this shrine. * The camp site of {{ill|Souryo Prince|ja|宗良親王}}. * A temizuya (water ablution pavilion) – Recently (in the 2010s) rebuilt with a ceiling mural depicting a {{ill|dragon|ja|龍}}. * A kaguraden (dancing hall). * A stone marker. * The sacred horse ({{ill|Shinme|ja|神馬}}). Kitano Tenjin Inari.jpg|Inari Shrine Kitano Tenjin Yagumo.jpg|Yakumo Shrine KitanoTenjin AyakoJinja.jpg|Fumiko Tenjin Shrine Kotesashi-jinja 14.jpg|Kotesashi Jinja and Kōkūjinja ; Trees and Other Features * The "Mikotozakura" cherry tree – Said to have been planted by {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|ヤマトタケル}}, this tree repeatedly dies and regrows. * The "Dainagon Ume" – Planted in the 18th year of the {{ill|Tenshō Era|ja|天正}} (1590) by {{ill|Maeda Toshiie|ja|前田利家}}, currently in its second generation as of 2015. It is named for Maeda Toshiie's former rank, {{ill|Dainagon|ja|大納言}}, and commemorates his revival of the shrine during the 【ill|Odawara Campaign|ja|小田原攻め】. * A stone monument (addressed "Kitano") – Established on September 25, {{ill|Heisei|ja|平成}} 18 (2006); it notes that the surrounding area "Kitano" derives its name from the shrine. * The camp site of {{ill|Souryo Prince|ja|宗良親王}}. * A hand-washing basin (temizuya) – Recently rebuilt (in the 2010s) with a ceiling mural depicting a dragon. * A kaguraden (dancing hall). * A power stone. * A divine horse ({{ill|Shinme|ja|神馬}}). Dainagon-ume Kitano-Tenjin-sha.jpg|Dainagon Ume Kitano Tenjin shinme.jpg|Sacred Horse == Cultural Properties == === Saitama Prefecture-designated Cultural Properties === * Tangible Cultural Property: ** Kitano Tenjin Shrine Engi (Origin Legend) (paintings) – Comprising 7 silk-colored hanging scrolls and 7 old logs.{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.city.tokorozawa.saitama.jp/iitokoro/enjoy/bunkakyoyo/bunkazai/kenshiteibunkazai/bunzai_20100510170056823.html |title=北野天神社縁起 付 旧軸木七本 |publisher=Tokorozawa City Education Committee, Cultural Property Protection Division |accessdate=2015-06}} === Tokorozawa City-designated Cultural Properties === * Tangible Cultural Property: ** The Ume Song Monument of Kitano Tenjin Shrine (a scenic spot) – Established in the 2nd year of the {{ill|Kyōwa|ja|享和}} era (1802); it is the oldest song monument in the city.{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.city.tokorozawa.saitama.jp/iitokoro/enjoy/bunkakyoyo/bunkazai/shishiteibunkazai/meisyo/bunzai_20100601150043467.html |title=尊桜の歌碑 |publisher=Tokorozawa City Education Committee, Cultural Property Protection Division |accessdate=2015-06}} ** Medieval Documents of Kitano Tenjin Shrine – A collection of 11 documents including a donation letter from the Ashikaga clan.{{Cite web|和書|url=https://www.city.tokorozawa.saitama.jp/iitokoro/enjoy/bunkakyoyo/bunkazai/shishiteibunkazai/komonjo/bunzai_20100810104554996.html |title=北野天神社中世文書 |publisher=Tokorozawa City Education Committee, Cultural Property Protection Division |accessdate=2015-06}} == Concurrent Shrines == * {{ill|Fujimori Inari Shrine (Tokorozawa)|ja|藤森稲荷神社 (所沢市)}} * {{ill|Rokusho Shrine (Tokorozawa)|ja|六所神社 (所沢市)}} * {{ill|Suwa Shrine (Tokorozawa)|ja|諏訪神社 (所沢市)}} – Located at 1-17-21 Kotesashi. Suwa Jinja Kotesashi.jpg|Suwa Shrine == List of Festivals == * New Year Festival (元旦祭, January 1) – Ritual talismans ("祈祷札") are distributed. * Hatsumōde (初詣) (January 1) * Setsubun Festival (節分祭, February 3) – Corresponds to the Ōharae at Kitano Tenjin Shrine; the "Shikinaisha Kitano Shrine Ōharae Shinpū" is distributed. * Hatsu-uma Festival (初午祭, February 11) – Held at the Inari Shrine within the precincts; "Inari Shrine Shinpū" is distributed. * Kinen-sai (祈年祭, February 27) – Also known as "Toshigoi no Matsuri"; "Kinen-sai Shinpū" is distributed. * Spring Seasonal Festival (春季例大祭, March 21) – Paired with the autumn festival, this is the most important festival at the shrine; "Kuniichi Jigisha Kaiun Shugoshinpū" is distributed. * Spring Festival (春祭, March 25) – Also called "Nibanmachi"; "Mononobe Tenjinsha Shinpū" is distributed. * Sericulture Festival (養蚕祭, April 3) – Held at the Bunkoten Shrine within the precincts; "Bunkoten Shrine Shinpū" is distributed. * Memorial Festival (慰霊祭, April 15) – Held at the Kotesashi Jinja to commemorate war dead from the Nisshin and Nichiro periods. * Yakumo Festival (八雲祭) – Held on the evening of July 14 and main festival on July 15; "Yakumo Shrine Prayer Talisman for Disaster Exorcism" is distributed. * Autumn Seasonal Festival (秋季例大祭, Late September) – Annual musical offerings and a village kagura are performed biennially. * Niiname-sai (新嘗祭, November 23) – "Niiname-sai Shinpū" is distributed.{{Cite web|和書|url=https://kitanotenjin.com/nenkangyouji.html |title=北野天神社のお祭り |publisher=Kitano Tenjin Shrine |accessdate=2022-01-15}} == Footnotes == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} == References == * Tokorozawa City Historical Research No.3 [https://www.city.tokorozawa.saitama.jp/iitokoro/enjoy/rekishi/sisi02.html About the Kitano Tenjin Shrine Engi Picture] (Author: Nakahara Nakatomo) == Further Reading == * {{cite book|和書|title=[[Shinpen Musashi Fudoki-kō]]|volume=巻ノ158 入間郡ノ3|chapter=Kitano-mura the precincts; "Inari Shrine Shinpū" is distributed. * Kinen-sai (祈年祭, February 27) – Also known as "Toshigoi no Matsuri"; "Kinen-sai Shinpū" is distributed. * Spring Seasonal Festival (春季例大祭, March 21) – Paired with the autumn festival, this is the most important festival at the shrine; "Kuniichi Jigisha Kaiun Shugoshinpū" is distributed. * Spring Festival (春祭, March 25) – Also called Festival (慰霊祭, April 15) – Held at Kotesashi Jinja to commemorate war dead from the Nisshin and Nichiro periods. * Yakumo Festival (八雲祭) – Held on the evening of July 14 (yo-miya) and the main Haiden |所在地 = {{ill|Saitama Prefecture|ja|埼玉県}}{{ill|Tokorozawa City|ja|所沢市}}{{ill|Kotesashi Motomachi|ja|小手指元町}} 3-28-44 |位置 = {{Coord|35|47|26.0|N|139|25|43.3|E|region:JP-11_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name={{ill|Kitano Tenjin Shrine|ja|北野天神社}}}} |祭神 = {{ill|Nigihayahi|ja|ニギハヤヒ}} (Kushitama Nigi Hayahito)
{{ill|Okunitama|ja|大国主}} (Yachihoko no Mikoto)
{{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|ja|Sugawara no Michizane}} |社格 = {{ill|Engishiki Shinmeichō|ja|延喜式神名帳}} (Shikinaisha; subsidiary shrines: two of the smaller class and one of the larger class)
{{ill|Kensha|ja|県社}} |創建 = Unknown |本殿 = |別名 = Kitano Tenjin Shrine (collective name) |例祭 = {{ill|March 21|ja|3月21日}} (Spring Annual Festival) |神事 = |地図 = {{Location map|Japan Saitama|label={{ill|Kitano Tenjin Shrine|ja|北野天神社}}|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20|float=center|border=none|position=top|width=210|caption=}} {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=12|frame-align=center|frame-width=210}} }} [[File:Kitano-Tenjin-sha sandō.jpg|thumb|Kitano Tenjin Shrine, South Approach Path]] '''Kitano Tenjin Shrine''' ({{ill|Kitano Tenjin Shrine|ja|北野天神社}}, きたのてんじんじゃ) is a Shinto shrine located in {{ill|Saitama Prefecture|ja|埼玉県}}, {{ill|Tokorozawa City|ja|所沢市}}, {{ill|Kotesashi Motomachi|ja|小手指元町}}. It is classified as a Shikinaisha (as recorded in the {{ill|Engishiki Shinmeichō|ja|延喜式神名帳}}; two subsidiary shrines of the smaller class and one of the larger class), and under the former modern shrine ranking system it held the rank of Prefectural Shrine. The registered name of the religious corporation is '''{{ill|Mononobe Tenjin Shrine|ja|物部天神社}}・{{ill|Kuniichi Jigishinja|ja|國渭地祇神社}}・{{ill|Tenmantenjinja|ja|天満天神社}}'''; "Kitano Tenjin Shrine" is the collective term for these shrines.{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.city.tokorozawa.saitama.jp/iitokoro/enjoy/kids/shokai/meisyokyuseki/kitanotenjinsya.html |title={{ill|Kitano Tenjin Shrine|ja|北野天神社}} (Kitano) |date=2008-10-31 |publisher=Tokorozawa City Education Committee, Cultural Property Protection Division |accessdate=2015-06}} == 祭神 == * {{ill|Mononobe Tenjin Shrine|ja|物部天神社}} (もののべてんじんじゃ): Enshrines {{ill|Nigihayahi|ja|ニギハヤヒ}} (にぎはやひのみこと) – designated as the subsidiary shrine "Mononobe Tenjin Shrine", enshrining {{ill|Izumo Ihabishi Shrine|ja|出雲伊波比神社}} in conjunction. * {{ill|Kuniichi Jigishinja|ja|国渭地祇神社}} (くにいちぎじんじゃ): Enshrines {{ill|Okunitama|ja|大国主}} (やちほこのかみ) – designated as the subsidiary shrine "Kuniichi Jigisha". * {{ill|Tenmantenjinja|ja|天満天神社}} (てんまんてんじんじゃ): Enshrines {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|ja|Sugawara no Michizane}}. === 合祀 === * {{ill|Souryo Prince|ja|宗良親王}} (むねよししんのう) * {{ill|Kotesashi Myojin|ja|小手指明神}} * {{ill|Ameno Hohi|ja|アメノホヒ}} (あめのほひのみこと) * {{ill|Oujin Tennō|ja|応神天皇}} * {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|日本武尊命}} (やまとたけるのみこと) * {{ill|Ukano Mitama|ja|ウカノミタマ}} (うかのみたまのみこと)神社前 北野天神社略記.北野天神社.2022年1月15日閲覧 == History == According to shrine tradition, it is said that {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|日本武尊|1=Yamato Takeru|lt=Prince Yamato Takeru|3=ヤマトタケル}} enshrined this site during his eastern expedition. In the Edo period, the Edo Bakufu granted {{ill|Shuinjo|ja|朱印状}} to the shrine. * The Mononobe Tenjin Shrine served as the tutelary shrine of the Mononobe clan (see {{ill|Mujashi Kunizukuri|ja|无邪志国造}} for details on the clan) and still enshrines their ancestral deity, {{ill|Nigihayahi|ja|ニギハヤヒ}}. * As a Tenjin shrine, it was established in the first year of the {{ill|Chōtoku|ja|長徳}} era (995) when {{ill|Sugawara no Shūsei|ja|菅原修成}}, a fifth-generation descendant of {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|ja|Sugawara no Michizane}}, was commissioned as {{ill|Musashi-no-Mori|ja|武蔵守}} from Kyoto’s {{ill|Kitano Tenmangu|ja|北野天満宮}}; thereafter, the shrine buildings were constructed under the auspices of figures such as {{ill|Minamoto no Yoshiie|ja|源義家}}, {{ill|Minamoto no Yoritomo|ja|源頼朝}}, {{ill|Ashikaga Takauji|ja|足利尊氏}}, and {{ill|Maeda Toshiie|ja|前田利家}}. * Edo Shukkai-chō – From April 1 to 6 in the 7th year of the {{ill|Kyōhō|ja|享保}} era (1722), an opening ceremony for the shrine’s sacred object was held at the former {{ill|Mejiro Fudōin Hasedera|ja|目白不動院長谷寺}} in Edo, and on April 24 during that period, shrine treasures such as hanging scrolls and documents were submitted to Edo Castle at the shogun’s behest.{{Cite web|和書|url=https://www.asahi-net.or.jp/~hm9k-ajm/musasinorekisi/gosikifudoutomusasino/mejirofudou/kitanotennjinndekaityou/kitanotennjinnsyadekaityou.htm |title=北野天神社江戸出開帳 |work=おたまじゃくし |date=2001-11-11 |publisher=Yasushima Kiichi|accessdate=2015-06}} == Shrine Grounds == The shrine grounds feature an approach path lined with {{ill|torii|ja|鳥居}} and {{ill|stone lanterns|ja|石灯籠}} on the west and south sides. The west side faces the old {{ill|Kamakura Kaidō|ja|鎌倉街道}}, which runs north–south, and from the south side along {{ill|Saitama-Tokyo Road 179|ja|県道179号線}}, multiple staircases and torii lead up to the area in front of the haiden (worship hall). ; Shrines Within the Grounds * {{ill|Inari Shrine|ja|稲荷社}} * {{ill|Yakumo Shrine|ja|八雲社}} * {{ill|Kōkūjinja (Tokorozawa)|ja|航空神社}} – Established on September 25, Showa 12 by {{ill|Tokugawa Yoshitoshi|ja|徳川好敏}} at the {{ill|Tokorozawa Army Airfield|ja|所沢陸軍飛行場}}. Its establishment was prompted by the plight of aviation personnel who sacrificed their lives for the development of national aviation yet were not enshrined at {{ill|Yasukuni Shrine|ja|靖国神社}}. In Showa 13, with the founding of the {{ill|Army Air Officer Academy|ja|陸軍航空士官学校}}, the shrine was relocated from Tokorozawa to Toyooka (present-day {{ill|Iruma Base|ja|入間基地}}). On September 3, Showa 20, before the academy site was seized by the U.S. military, the shrine was re-situated within its current grounds. * {{ill|Fumiko Tenjin Shrine|ja|文子天神社}} – Enshrines Fumiko, who served as the wet nurse ({{ill|wet nurse|ja|乳母}}) of {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|ja|Sugawara no Michizane}}, known as {{ill|Tajihi Fumiko|ja|多治比文子}}. * {{ill|Kotesashi Jinja|ja|小手指神社}} – Enshrines the war dead (heroic spirits) of the Kotesashi area. The Mononobe Tenjinsha served as the ancestral shrine for the Mononobe clan. The Tenjinsha was established in 995 AD by Sugawara no Shusei, a descendant of Sugawara no Michizane, who enshrined the deity from Kitano Shrine in Kyoto. The shrine received official recognition from the Tokugawa Shogunate and saw contributions from historical figures such as Minamoto no Yoshiie, Minamoto no Yoritomo, Ashikaga Takauji, and Maeda Toshiie. == Festivals and Rituals == * '''New Year's Festival (January 1)''' * '''Setsubun Festival (February 3)''' * '''Hatsuuma Festival (February 11)''' * '''Kinensai (February 27)''' * '''Spring Grand Festival (March 21)''' * '''Spring Festival (March 25)''' * '''Silkworm Festival (April 3)''' * '''Memorial Service (April 15)''' * '''Yakumo Festival (July 14-15)''' * '''Autumn Grand Festival (Late September)''' * '''Niinamesai (November 23)''' == Cultural Properties == * '''Saitama Prefecture Designated Cultural Property:''' Kitano Tenjin Engi (painted scroll) * '''Tokorozawa City Designated Cultural Property:''' ** Song Monument of Mikoto Sakura ** Medieval documents related to Kitano Tenjinsha == Associated Shrines == * Fujimori Inari Jinja * Rokusho Jinja * Suwa Jinja == Notable Features == * Mikoto Sakura (Sacred Cherry Tree) * Dainagon Plum Tree (planted by Maeda Toshiie) * Ayako Tenjinsha (dedicated to Sugawara no Michizane's wet nurse) * Aviation Shrine (relocated from the former Tokorozawa Army Airfield) == Access Information == Kitano Tenjinsha is accessible from Kotesashi Station with a short walk. == External Links == * [Official Website](https://kitanotenjin.com/) * [Saitama Shrine Association](https://www.saitama-jinjacho.or.jp/shrine/8910/) {{神社 |名称 = {{ill|Mononobe Tenjinsha|ja|物部天神社}}・{{ill|Kuniichi Jigishinja|ja|国渭地祇神社}}

{{ill|Kensha|ja|県社}} |創建 = 不明 |本殿 = |別名 = 北野天神社（総称） |例祭 = {{ill|March 21|ja|3月21日}}（春の例大祭） |神事 = |地図 = {{Location map|Japan Saitama|label={{ill|Kitano Tenjin Shrine|ja|北野天神社}}|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20|float=center|border=none|position=top|width=210|caption=}} {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=12|frame-align=center|frame-width=210}} }} [[File:Kitano-Tenjin-sha sandō.jpg|thumb|北野天神社 南側参道にて]] '''Kitano Tenjin Shrine''' (北野天神社, きたのてんじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto Shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Saitama Prefecture|ja|埼玉県}}, {{ill|Tokorozawa City|ja|所沢市}}, {{ill|Kotesashi Motomachi|ja|小手指元町}}. It is classified as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} (two subsidiary shrines of the smaller class and one of the larger class according to the system of the {{ill|Engishiki Shinmeichō|ja|延喜式神名帳}}), with its former ranking under the modern shrine ranking system being that of a {{ill|Kensha|ja|県社}}. The registered name of the religious corporation is '''{{ill|Mononobe Tenjinsha|ja|物部天神社}}・{{ill|Kuniichi Jigishinja|ja|國渭地祇神社}}・{{ill|Tenmantenjinja|ja|天満天神社}}'''; "Kitano Tenjin Shrine" is a collective term for these shrines.{{Cite web|and=|url=http://www.city.tokorozawa.saitama.jp/iitokoro/enjoy/kids/shokai/meisyokyuseki/kitanotenjinsya.html |title=北野天神社（きたのてんじんしゃ）（北野） |date=2008-10-31 |publisher=Tokorozawa City Education Committee, Cultural Property Protection Division |accessdate=2015-06}} == 祭神 == * {{ill|Mononobe Tenjinsha|ja|物部天神社}} (もののべてんじんじゃ): Enshrines {{ill|Nigihayahi|ja|ニギハヤヒ|lt=Kushitama Nigi Hayahito|lt_ja=饒速日命}}, designated as the subsidiary shrine "Mononobe Tenjinsha" within the system; it is enshrined together with {{ill|Izumo Ihabishi Shrine|ja|出雲伊波比神社}}. * {{ill|Kuniichi Jigishinja|ja|国渭地祇神社}} (くにいちぎじんじゃ): Enshrines {{ill|Okunitama|ja|大国主|lt=Yachihoko no Mikoto|lt_ja=八千矛命}}, designated as the subsidiary shrine "Kuniichi Jigisha" ({{ill|Izumo Ihabishi Shrine|ja|出雲伊波比神社}} is enshrined together). * {{ill|Tenmantenjinja|ja|天満天神社}} (てんまんてんじんじゃ): Enshrines {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|ja|Sugawara no Michizane}}. === 合祀 === * {{ill|Souryo Prince|ja|宗良親王}} (むねよししんのう) * {{ill|Kotesashi Myojin|ja|小手指明神}} * {{ill|Ameno Hohi|ja|アメノホヒ|lt=Amenohohi no Mikoto|lt_ja=天穂日命}} * {{ill|Oujin Tennō|ja|応神天皇|lt=Emperor Ojin|lt_ja=應神天皇}} * {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|ヤマトタケル|lt=Prince Yamato Takeru|lt_ja=日本武尊命}} * {{ill|Ukano Mitama|ja|ウカノミタマ|lt=Ukano Mitama no Mikoto|lt_ja=倉稲魂命}} == History == According to shrine tradition, it is said that {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|日本武尊|1=Yamato Takeru|lt=Prince Yamato Takeru|3=ヤマトタケル}} enshrined this site during his eastern expedition. In the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, the Edo Bakufu granted {{ill|Shuinjo|ja|朱印状}} to the shrine. * The Mononobe Tenjinsha was the tutelary shrine of the Mononobe clan (see {{ill|Mujashi Kunizukuri|ja|无邪志国造}} for the family) and continues to enshrine their ancestral deity, {{ill|Nigihayahi|ja|ニギハヤヒ}}. * As a Tenjin Shrine, it was first enshrined by {{ill|Sugawara no Shūsei|ja|菅原修成}}, a 5th-generation descendant of {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|ja|Sugawara no Michizane}}, in the first year of the {{ill|Chōtoku|ja|長徳}} era (995) as a guardian in his capacity as {{ill|Musashi-no-Mori|ja|武蔵守}}, sent from Kyoto's {{ill|Kitano Tenmangu|ja|北野天満宮|lt=Kitano Shrine|lt_ja=北野神社}}. Subsequently, the shrine buildings were constructed under the auspices of figures such as {{ill|Minamoto no Yoshiie|ja|源義家}}, {{ill|Minamoto no Yoritomo|ja|源頼朝}}, {{ill|Ashikaga Takauji|ja|足利尊氏}}, and {{ill|Maeda Toshiie|ja|前田利家}}. * Edo Shukkai-chō – From April 1 to 6 in the 7th year of the {{ill|Kyōhō|ja|享保}} era (1722), an opening ceremony ({{ill|Shukkai-chō|ja|出開帳}}) for the shrine's sacred object was held at the former {{ill|Mejiro Fudōin Hasedera|ja|目白不動院長谷寺}} in Edo, and on April 24 during that period, temple treasures such as hanging scrolls and documents were submitted to Edo Castle at the behest of the shogun.{{Cite web|和書|url=https://www.asahi-net.or.jp/~hm9k-ajm/musasinorekisi/gosikifudoutomusasino/mejirofudou/kitanotennjinndekaityou/kitanotennjinnsyadekaityou.htm |title=北野天神社江戸出開帳 |work=おたまじゃくし |date=2001-11-11 |publisher=Yasushima Kiichi|accessdate=2015-06}} == Shrine Grounds == Within the shrine precincts, a sanmichi (approach path) lined with {{ill|torii|ja|鳥居}} and {{ill|stone lanterns|ja|石灯籠}} is located on the west and south sides. The west side faces the old {{ill|Kamakura Kaidō|ja|鎌倉街道}}, which runs north–south, and from the south side along {{ill|Saitama-Tokyo Road 179|ja|県道179号線}}, multiple staircases and torii lead up to the haiden (worship hall). ; Shrines Within the Grounds * {{ill|Inari Shrine|ja|稲荷社}} * {{ill|Yakumo Shrine|ja|八雲社}} * {{ill|Kōkūjinja (Tokorozawa)|ja|航空神社}} – Established on September 25, Showa 12 by {{ill|Tokugawa Yoshitoshi|ja|徳川好敏}}, at the {{ill|Tokorozawa Army Airfield|ja|所沢陸軍飛行場}}. Its establishment was inspired by the plight of aviation personnel who sacrificed their lives for the development of national aviation yet were not enshrined at {{ill|Yasukuni Shrine|ja|靖国神社}}; it was thus determined that a guardian deity for national aviation should be enshrined. In Showa 13, with the founding of the {{ill|Army Air Officer Academy|ja|陸軍航空士官学校}}, the shrine was relocated from Tokorozawa to Toyooka (present-day {{ill|Iruma Base|ja|入間基地}}). On September 3, Showa 20, before the academy site was seized by the U.S. military, the shrine was re-situated within its present grounds. * {{ill|Fumiko Tenjin Shrine|ja|文子天神社}} – Enshrines Fumiko, who served as the wet nurse ({{ill|wet nurse|ja|乳母}}) of {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|ja|Sugawara no Michizane}}, known as {{ill|Tajihi Fumiko|ja|多治比文子}}. * {{ill|Kotesashi Jinja|ja|小手指神社}} – Enshrines the war dead (heroic spirits) of the Kotesashi area. ; Trees on the Grounds * {{ill|Mikotozakura|ja|尊桜}} – A cherry tree said to have been planted in front of the shrine by {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|ヤマトタケル}}, which repeatedly dies and regrows (exhibiting {{ill|Noda|ja|蘖（ひこばえ）}}). * {{ill|Dainagon Ume|ja|大納言梅}} – Planted in the 18th year of the {{ill|Tenshō Era|ja|天正}} (1590) by {{ill|Maeda Toshiie|ja|前田利家}}, currently the second generation as of 2015. It is said that Maeda Toshiie, who claimed descent from {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|ja|Sugawara no Michizane}} and used the Ume crest ({{ill|Ume Crest|ja|梅紋}}), revived the shrine by planting a single plum tree during the 【ill|Odawara Campaign|ja|小田原攻め】; his title at that time was {{ill|Dainagon|ja|大納言}}. ; Other Elements Within the Grounds * A stone monument recording the origin of the local name "Kitano" – Established on September 25, {{ill|Heisei|ja|平成}} 18 (2006). Although recent land reorganization has changed the shrine's address to Kotesashi Motomachi, the surrounding area retains the name "Kitano" as derived from this shrine. * The camp site of {{ill|Souryo Prince|ja|宗良親王}}. * A temizuya (water ablution pavilion) – Recently (in the 2010s) rebuilt with a ceiling mural depicting a {{ill|dragon|ja|龍}}. * A kaguraden (dancing hall). * A stone marker. * The sacred horse ({{ill|Shinme|ja|神馬}}). Kitano Tenjin Inari.jpg|Inari Shrine Kitano Tenjin Yagumo.jpg|Yakumo Shrine KitanoTenjin AyakoJinja.jpg|Fumiko Tenjin Shrine Kotesashi-jinja 14.jpg|Kotesashi Jinja and Kōkūjinja ; Trees and Other Features * The "Mikotozakura" cherry tree – Said to have been planted by {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|ヤマトタケル}}, this tree repeatedly dies and regrows. * The "Dainagon Ume" – Planted in the 18th year of the {{ill|Tenshō Era|ja|天正}} (1590) by {{ill|Maeda Toshiie|ja|前田利家}}, currently in its second generation as of 2015. It is named for Maeda Toshiie's former rank, {{ill|Dainagon|ja|大納言}}, and commemorates his revival of the shrine during the 【ill|Odawara Campaign|ja|小田原攻め】. * A stone monument (addressed "Kitano") – Established on September 25, {{ill|Heisei|ja|平成}} 18 (2006); it notes that the surrounding area "Kitano" derives its name from the shrine. * The camp site of {{ill|Souryo Prince|ja|宗良親王}}. * A hand-washing basin (temizuya) – Recently rebuilt (in the 2010s) with a ceiling mural depicting a dragon. * A kaguraden (dancing hall). * A power stone. * A divine horse ({{ill|Shinme|ja|神馬}}). Dainagon-ume Kitano-Tenjin-sha.jpg|Dainagon Ume Kitano Tenjin shinme.jpg|Sacred Horse == Cultural Properties == === Saitama Prefecture-designated Cultural Properties === * Tangible Cultural Property: ** Kitano Tenjin Shrine Engi (Origin Legend) (paintings) – Comprising 7 silk-colored hanging scrolls and 7 old logs.{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.city.tokorozawa.saitama.jp/iitokoro/enjoy/bunkakyoyo/bunkazai/kenshiteibunkazai/bunzai_20100510170056823.html |title=北野天神社縁起 付 旧軸木七本 |publisher=Tokorozawa City Education Committee, Cultural Property Protection Division |accessdate=2015-06}} === Tokorozawa City-designated Cultural Properties === * Tangible Cultural Property: ** The Ume Song Monument of Kitano Tenjin Shrine (a scenic spot) – Established in the 2nd year of the {{ill|Kyōwa|ja|享和}} era (1802); it is the oldest song monument in the city.{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.city.tokorozawa.saitama.jp/iitokoro/enjoy/bunkakyoyo/bunkazai/shishiteibunkazai/meisyo/bunzai_20100601150043467.html |title=尊桜の歌碑 |publisher=Tokorozawa City Education Committee, Cultural Property Protection Division |accessdate=2015-06}} ** Medieval Documents of Kitano Tenjin Shrine – A collection of 11 documents including a donation letter from the Ashikaga clan.{{Cite web|和書|url=https://www.city.tokorozawa.saitama.jp/iitokoro/enjoy/bunkakyoyo/bunkazai/shishiteibunkazai/komonjo/bunzai_20100810104554996.html |title=北野天神社中世文書 |publisher=Tokorozawa City Education Committee, Cultural Property Protection Division |accessdate=2015-06}} == Concurrent Shrines == * {{ill|Fujimori Inari Shrine (Tokorozawa)|ja|藤森稲荷神社 (所沢市)}} * {{ill|Rokusho Shrine (Tokorozawa)|ja|六所神社 (所沢市)}} * {{ill|Suwa Shrine (Tokorozawa)|ja|諏訪神社 (所沢市)}} – Located at 1-17-21 Kotesashi. Suwa Jinja Kotesashi.jpg|Suwa Shrine == List of Festivals == * New Year Festival (元旦祭, January 1) – Ritual talismans ("祈祷札") are distributed. * Hatsumōde (初詣) (January 1) * Setsubun Festival (節分祭, February 3) – Corresponds to the Ōharae at Kitano Tenjin Shrine; the "Shikinaisha Kitano Shrine Ōharae Shinpū" is distributed. * Hatsu-uma Festival (初午祭, February 11) – Held at the Inari Shrine within the precincts; "Inari Shrine Shinpū" is distributed. * Kinen-sai (祈年祭, February 27) – Also known as "Toshigoi no Matsuri"; "Kinen-sai Shinpū" is distributed. * Spring Seasonal Festival (春季例大祭, March 21) – Paired with the autumn festival, this is the most important festival at the shrine; "Kuniichi Jigisha Kaiun Shugoshinpū" is distributed. * Spring Festival (春祭, March 25) – Also called "Nibanmachi"; "Mononobe Tenjinsha Shinpū" is distributed. * Sericulture Festival (養蚕祭, April 3) – Held at the Bunkoten Shrine within the precincts; "Bunkoten Shrine Shinpū" is distributed. * Memorial Festival (慰霊祭, April 15) – Held at the Kotesashi Jinja to commemorate war dead from the Nisshin and Nichiro periods. * Yakumo Festival (八雲祭) – Held on the evening of July 14 and main festival on July 15; "Yakumo Shrine Prayer Talisman for Disaster Exorcism" is distributed. * Autumn Seasonal Festival (秋季例大祭, Late September) – Annual musical offerings and a village kagura are performed biennially. * Niiname-sai (新嘗祭, November 23) – "Niiname-sai Shinpū" is distributed.{{Cite web|和書|url=https://kitanotenjin.com/nenkangyouji.html |title=北野天神社のお祭り |publisher=Kitano Tenjin Shrine {{ill|Kensha|ja|県社}} |創建 = Unknown |本殿 = |別名 = Kitano Tenjin Shrine (collective name) |例祭 = {{ill|March 21|ja|3月21日}} (Spring Annual Festival) |神事 = |地図 = {{Location map|Japan Saitama|label={{ill|Kitano Tenjin Shrine|ja|北野天神社}}|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20|float=center|border=none|position=top|width=210|caption=}} {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=12|frame-align=center|frame-width=210}} }} [[File:Kitano-Tenjin-sha sandō.jpg|thumb|Kitano Tenjin Shrine, South Approach Path]] '''Kitano Tenjin Shrine''' ({{ill|Kitano Tenjin Shrine|ja|北野天神社}}, きたのてんじんじゃ) is a Shinto shrine located in {{ill|Saitama Prefecture|ja|埼玉県}}, {{ill|Tokorozawa City|ja|所沢市}}, {{ill|Kotesashi Motomachi|ja|小手指元町}}. It is classified as a Shikinaisha (as recorded in the {{ill|Engishiki Shinmeichō|ja|延喜式神名帳}}; two subsidiary shrines of the smaller class and one of the larger class), and under the former modern shrine ranking system it held the rank of Prefectural Shrine. The registered name of the religious corporation is '''{{ill|Mononobe Tenjin Shrine|ja|物部天神社}}・{{ill|Kuniichi Jigishinja|ja|國渭地祇神社}}・{{ill|Tenmantenjinja|ja|天満天神社}}'''; "Kitano Tenjin Shrine" is the collective term for these shrines.{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.city.tokorozawa.saitama.jp/iitokoro/enjoy/kids/shokai/meisyokyuseki/kitanotenjinsya.html |title={{ill|Kitano Tenjin Shrine|ja|北野天神社}} (Kitano) |date=2008-10-31 |publisher=Tokorozawa City Education Committee, Cultural Property Protection Division |accessdate=2015-06}} == 祭神 == * {{ill|Mononobe Tenjin Shrine|ja|物部天神社}} (もののべてんじんじゃ): Enshrines {{ill|Nigihayahi|ja|ニギハヤヒ}} (にぎはやひのみこと) – designated as the subsidiary shrine "Mononobe Tenjin Shrine", enshrining {{ill|Izumo Ihabishi Shrine|ja|出雲伊波比神社}} in conjunction. * {{ill|Kuniichi Jigishinja|ja|国渭地祇神社}} (くにいちぎじんじゃ): Enshrines {{ill|Okunitama|ja|大国主}} (やちほこのかみ) – designated as the subsidiary shrine "Kuniichi Jigisha". * {{ill|Tenmantenjinja|ja|天満天神社}} (てんまんてんじんじゃ): Enshrines {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|ja|Sugawara no Michizane}}. === 合祀 === * {{ill|Souryo Prince|ja|宗良親王}} (むねよししんのう) * {{ill|Kotesashi Myojin|ja|小手指明神}} * {{ill|Ameno Hohi|ja|アメノホヒ}} (あめのほひのみこと) * {{ill|Oujin Tennō|ja|応神天皇}} * {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|日本武尊命}} (やまとたけるのみこと) * {{ill|Ukano Mitama|ja|ウカノミタマ}} (うかのみたまのみこと)神社前 北野天神社略記.北野天神社.2022年1月15日閲覧 == History == According to shrine tradition, it is said that {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|日本武尊|1=Yamato Takeru|lt=Prince Yamato Takeru|3=ヤマトタケル}} enshrined this site during his eastern expedition. In the Edo period, the Edo Bakufu granted {{ill|Shuinjo|ja|朱印状}} to the shrine. * The Mononobe Tenjin Shrine served as the tutelary shrine of the Mononobe clan (see {{ill|Mujashi Kunizukuri|ja|无邪志国造}} for details on the clan) and still enshrines their ancestral deity, {{ill|Nigihayahi|ja|ニギハヤヒ}}. * As a Tenjin shrine, it was established in the first year of the {{ill|Chōtoku|ja|長徳}} era (995) when {{ill|Sugawara no Shūsei|ja|菅原修成}}, a fifth-generation descendant of {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|ja|Sugawara no Michizane}}, was commissioned as {{ill|Musashi-no-Mori|ja|武蔵守}} from Kyoto’s {{ill|Kitano Tenmangu|ja|北野天満宮}}; thereafter, the shrine buildings were constructed under the auspices of figures such as {{ill|Minamoto no Yoshiie|ja|源義家}}, {{ill|Minamoto no Yoritomo|ja|源頼朝}}, {{ill|Ashikaga Takauji|ja|足利尊氏}}, and {{ill|Maeda Toshiie|ja|前田利家}}. * Edo Shukkai-chō – From April 1 to 6 in the 7th year of the {{ill|Kyōhō|ja|享保}} era (1722), an opening ceremony for the shrine’s sacred object was held at the former {{ill|Mejiro Fudōin Hasedera|ja|目白不動院長谷寺}} in Edo, and on April 24 during that period, shrine treasures such as hanging scrolls and documents were submitted to Edo Castle at the shogun’s behest.{{Cite web|和書|url=https://www.asahi-net.or.jp/~hm9k-ajm/musasinorekisi/gosikifudoutomusasino/mejirofudou/kitanotennjinndekaityou/kitanotennjinnsyadekaityou.htm |title=北野天神社江戸出開帳 |work=おたまじゃくし |date=2001-11-11 |publisher=Yasushima Kiichi|accessdate=2015-06}} == Shrine Grounds == The shrine grounds feature an approach path lined with {{ill|torii|ja|鳥居}} and {{ill|stone lanterns|ja|石灯籠}} on the west and south sides. The west side faces the old {{ill|Kamakura Kaidō|ja|鎌倉街道}}, which runs north–south, and from the south side along {{ill|Saitama-Tokyo Road 179|ja|県道179号線}}, multiple staircases and torii lead up to the area in front of the haiden (worship hall). ; Shrines Within the Grounds * {{ill|Inari Shrine|ja|稲荷社}} * {{ill|Yakumo Shrine|ja|八雲社}} * {{ill|Kōkūjinja (Tokorozawa)|ja|航空神社}} – Established on September 25, Showa 12 by {{ill|Tokugawa Yoshitoshi|ja|徳川好敏}} at the {{ill|Tokorozawa Army Airfield|ja|所沢陸軍飛行場}}. Its establishment was prompted by the plight of aviation personnel who sacrificed their lives for the development of national aviation yet were not enshrined at {{ill|Yasukuni Shrine|ja|靖国神社}}. In Showa 13, with the founding of the {{ill|Army Air Officer Academy|ja|陸軍航空士官学校}}, the shrine was relocated from Tokorozawa to Toyooka (present-day {{ill|Iruma Base|ja|入間基地}}). On September 3, Showa 20, before the academy site was seized by the U.S. military, the shrine was re-situated within its current grounds. * {{ill|Fumiko Tenjin Shrine|ja|文子天神社}} – Enshrines Fumiko, who served as the wet nurse ({{ill|wet nurse|ja|乳母}}) of {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|ja|Sugawara no Michizane}}, known as {{ill|Tajihi Fumiko|ja|多治比文子}}. * {{ill|Kotesashi Jinja|ja|小手指神社}} – Enshrines the war dead (heroic spirits) of the Kotesashi area. Kitano Tenjin Inari.jpg|Inari Shrine Kitano Tenjin Yagumo.jpg|Yakumo Shrine KitanoTenjin AyakoJinja.jpg|Fumiko Tenjin Shrine Kotesashi-jinja 14.jpg|Kotesashi Jinja and Kōkūjinja ; Trees on the Grounds * {{ill|Mikoto-zakura|ja|尊桜}} – A cherry tree said to have been planted in front of the shrine by {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|ヤマトタケル}}, which repeatedly dies and regrows (exhibiting {{ill|nodate|ja|蘖（ひこばえ）}}). * {{ill|Dainagon Ume|ja|大納言梅}} – Planted in the 18th year of the {{ill|Tenshō Era|ja|天正}} (1590) by {{ill|Maeda Toshiie|ja|前田利家}}, currently in its second generation as of 2015. It is named after Maeda Toshiie’s former rank, {{ill|Dainagon|ja|大納言}}, commemorating his restoration of the shrine during the {{ill|Odawara Campaign|ja|小田原攻め}}. ; Other Elements Within the Grounds * A stone monument recording the origin of the local name “Kitano” – Established on September 25, {{ill|Heisei|ja|平成}} 18 (2006); it states that the surrounding area “Kitano” derives its name from this shrine. * The campsite of {{ill|Souryo Prince|ja|宗良親王}}. * A temizuya (water ablution pavilion) – Recently rebuilt (in the 2010s) with a ceiling mural depicting a {{ill|dragon|ja|龍}}. * A kaguraden (dancing hall). * A power stone. * A divine horse ({{ill|Shinme|ja|神馬}}). Dainagon-ume Kitano-Tenjin-sha.jpg|Dainagon Ume Kitano Tenjin shinme.jpg|Sacred Horse == Cultural Properties == === Saitama Prefecture-designated Cultural Properties === * Tangible Cultural Property: ** Kitano Tenjin Shrine Engi (Origin Legend) (paintings) – Consisting of 7 silk-colored hanging scrolls and 7 old logs.{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.city.tokorozawa.saitama.jp/iitokoro/enjoy/bunkakyoyo/bunkazai/kenshiteibunkazai/bunzai_20100510170056823.html |title=Kitano Tenjin Shrine Engi, with 7 old logs |publisher=Tokorozawa City Education Committee, Cultural Property Protection Division |accessdate=2015-06}} === Tokorozawa City-designated Cultural Properties === * Tangible Cultural Property: ** The Ume Song Monument of Kitano Tenjin Shrine (a scenic spot) – Established in the 2nd year of the {{ill|Kyōwa Era|ja|享和}} (1802); it is the oldest song monument in the city.{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.city.tokorozawa.saitama.jp/iitokoro/enjoy/bunkakyoyo/bunkazai/shishiteibunkazai/meisyo/bunzai_20100601150043467.html |title=尊桜の歌碑 |publisher=Tokorozawa City Education Committee, Cultural Property Protection Division |accessdate=2015-06}} ** Medieval Documents of Kitano Tenjin Shrine – A collection of 11 documents including a donation letter from the Ashikaga clan.{{Cite web|和書|url=https://www.city.tokorozawa.saitama.jp/iitokoro/enjoy/bunkakyoyo/bunkazai/shishiteibunkazai/komonjo/bunzai_20100810104554996.html |title=Kitano Tenjin Shrine Medieval Documents |publisher=Tokorozawa City Education Committee, Cultural Property Protection Division |accessdate=2015-06}} == Concurrent Shrines == * {{ill|Fujimori Inari Shrine (Tokorozawa)|ja|藤森稲荷神社 (所沢市)}} * {{ill|Rokusho Shrine (Tokorozawa)|ja|六所神社 (所沢市)}} * {{ill|Suwa Shrine (Tokorozawa)|ja|諏訪神社 (所沢市)}} – Located at 1-17-21 Kotesashi. Suwa Jinja Kotesashi.jpg|Suwa Shrine == List of Festivals == * New Year Festival (元旦祭, January 1) – "Prayer talismans" ("祈祷札") are distributed. * Hatsumōde (初詣) (January 1) * Setsubun Festival (節分祭, February 3) – Corresponds to the Ōharae at Kitano Tenjin Shrine; the "Shikinaisha Kitano Shrine Ōharae Shinpū" is distributed. * Hatsu-uma Festival (初午祭, February 11) – Held at the Inari Shrine within the precincts; "Inari Shrine Shinpū" is distributed. * Kinen-sai (祈年祭, February 27) – Also known as "Toshigoi no Matsuri"; "Kinen-sai Shinpū" is distributed. * Spring Seasonal Festival (春季例大祭, March 21) – Paired with the autumn festival, this is the most important festival at the shrine; "Kuniichi Jigisha Kaiun Shugoshinpū" is distributed. * Spring Festival (春祭, March 25) – Also called "Nibanmachi"; "Mononobe Tenjinsha Shinpū" is distributed. * Sericulture Festival (養蚕祭, April 3) – Held at the Bunkoten Shrine within the precincts; "Bunkoten Shrine Shinpū" is distributed. * Memorial Festival (慰霊祭, April 15) – Held at Kotesashi Jinja to commemorate war dead from the Nisshin and Nichiro periods. * Yakumo Festival (八雲祭) – Held on the evening of July 14 (yo-miya) and the main festival on July 15; "Yakumo Shrine Prayer Talisman for Disaster Exorcism" is distributed. * Autumn Seasonal Festival (秋季例大祭, Late September) – Musical offerings are made annually, and a village kagura is performed every two years. * Niiname-sai (新嘗祭, November 23) – "Niiname-sai Shinpū" is distributed.{{Cite web|和書|url=https://kitanotenjin.com/nenkangyouji.html |title=Kitano Tenjin Shrine The Mononobe Tenjinsha served as the ancestral shrine for the Mononobe clan. The Tenjinsha was established in 995 AD by Sugawara no Shusei, a descendant of Sugawara no Michizane, who enshrined the deity from Kitano Shrine in Kyoto. The shrine received official recognition from the Tokugawa Shogunate and saw contributions from historical figures such as Minamoto no Yoshiie, Minamoto no Yoritomo, Ashikaga Takauji, and Maeda Toshiie. == Festivals and Rituals == * '''New Year's Festival (January 1)''' * '''Setsubun Festival (February 3)''' * '''Hatsuuma Festival (February 11)''' * '''Kinensai (February 27)''' * '''Spring Grand Festival (March 21)''' * '''Spring Festival (March 25)''' * '''Silkworm Festival (April 3)''' * '''Memorial Service (April 15)''' * '''Yakumo Festival (July 14-15)''' * '''Autumn Grand Festival (Late September)''' * '''Niinamesai (November 23)''' == Cultural Properties == * '''Saitama Prefecture Designated Cultural Property:''' Kitano Tenjin Engi (painted scroll) * '''Tokorozawa City Designated Cultural Property:''' ** Song Monument of Mikoto Sakura ** Medieval documents related to Kitano Tenjinsha == Associated Shrines == * Fujimori Inari Jinja * Rokusho Jinja * Suwa Jinja == Notable Features == * Mikoto Sakura (Sacred Cherry Tree) * Dainagon Plum Tree (planted by Maeda Toshiie) * Ayako Tenjinsha (dedicated to Sugawara no Michizane's wet nurse) * Aviation Shrine (relocated from the former Tokorozawa Army Airfield) == Access Information == Kitano Tenjinsha is accessible from Kotesashi Station with a short walk. == External Links == * [Official Website](https://kitanotenjin.com/) * [Saitama Shrine Association](https://www.saitama-jinjacho.or.jp/shrine/8910/) {{神社 |名称 = {{ill|Mononobe Tenjinsha|ja|物部天神社}}・{{ill|Kuniichi Jigishinja|ja|国渭地祇神社}}

{{ill|Kensha|ja|県社}} |創建 = 不明 |本殿 = |別名 = 北野天神社（総称） |例祭 = {{ill|March 21|ja|3月21日}}（春の例大祭） |神事 = |地図 = {{Location map|Japan Saitama|label={{ill|Kitano Tenjin Shrine|ja|北野天神社}}|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20|float=center|border=none|position=top|width=210|caption=}} {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=12|frame-align=center|frame-width=210}} }} [[File:Kitano-Tenjin-sha sandō.jpg|thumb|北野天神社 南側参道にて]] '''Kitano Tenjin Shrine''' (北野天神社, きたのてんじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto Shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Saitama Prefecture|ja|埼玉県}}, {{ill|Tokorozawa City|ja|所沢市}}, {{ill|Kotesashi Motomachi|ja|小手指元町}}. It is classified as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} (two subsidiary shrines of the smaller class and one of the larger class according to the system of the {{ill|Engishiki Shinmeichō|ja|延喜式神名帳}}), with its former ranking under the modern shrine ranking system being that of a {{ill|Kensha|ja|県社}}. The registered name of the religious corporation is '''{{ill|Mononobe Tenjinsha|ja|物部天神社}}・{{ill|Kuniichi Jigishinja|ja|國渭地祇神社}}・{{ill|Tenmantenjinja|ja|天満天神社}}'''; "Kitano Tenjin Shrine" is a collective term for these shrines.{{Cite web|and=|url=http://www.city.tokorozawa.saitama.jp/iitokoro/enjoy/kids/shokai/meisyokyuseki/kitanotenjinsya.html |title=北野天神社（きたのてんじんしゃ）（北野） |date=2008-10-31 |publisher=Tokorozawa City Education Committee, Cultural Property Protection Division |accessdate=2015-06}} == 祭神 == * {{ill|Mononobe Tenjinsha|ja|物部天神社}} (もののべてんじんじゃ): Enshrines {{ill|Nigihayahi|ja|ニギハヤヒ|lt=Kushitama Nigi Hayahito|lt_ja=饒速日命}}, designated as the subsidiary shrine "Mononobe Tenjinsha" within the system; it is enshrined together with {{ill|Izumo Ihabishi Shrine|ja|出雲伊波比神社}}. * {{ill|Kuniichi Jigishinja|ja|国渭地祇神社}} (くにいちぎじんじゃ): Enshrines {{ill|Okunitama|ja|大国主|lt=Yachihoko no Mikoto|lt_ja=八千矛命}}, designated as the subsidiary shrine "Kuniichi Jigisha" ({{ill|Izumo Ihabishi Shrine|ja|出雲伊波比神社}} is enshrined together). * {{ill|Tenmantenjinja|ja|天満天神社}} (てんまんてんじんじゃ): Enshrines {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|ja|Sugawara no Michizane}}. === 合祀 === * {{ill|Souryo Prince|ja|宗良親王}} (むねよししんのう) * {{ill|Kotesashi Myojin|ja|小手指明神}} * {{ill|Ameno Hohi|ja|アメノホヒ|lt=Amenohohi no Mikoto|lt_ja=天穂日命}} * {{ill|Oujin Tennō|ja|応神天皇|lt=Emperor Ojin|lt_ja=應神天皇}} * {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|ヤマトタケル|lt=Prince Yamato Takeru|lt_ja=日本武尊命}} * {{ill|Ukano Mitama|ja|ウカノミタマ|lt=Ukano Mitama no Mikoto|lt_ja=倉稲魂命}} == History == According to shrine tradition, it is said that {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|日本武尊|1=Yamato Takeru|lt=Prince Yamato Takeru|3=ヤマトタケル}} enshrined this site during his eastern expedition. In the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, the Edo Bakufu granted {{ill|Shuinjo|ja|朱印状}} to the shrine. * The Mononobe Tenjinsha was the tutelary shrine of the Mononobe clan (see {{ill|Mujashi Kunizukuri|ja|无邪志国造}} for the family) and continues to enshrine their ancestral deity, {{ill|Nigihayahi|ja|ニギハヤヒ}}. * As a Tenjin Shrine, it was first enshrined by {{ill|Sugawara no Shūsei|ja|菅原修成}}, a 5th-generation descendant of {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|ja|Sugawara no Michizane}}, in the first year of the {{ill|Chōtoku|ja|長徳}} era (995) as a guardian in his capacity as {{ill|Musashi-no-Mori|ja|武蔵守}}, sent from Kyoto's {{ill|Kitano Tenmangu|ja|北野天満宮|lt=Kitano Shrine|lt_ja=北野神社}}. Subsequently, the shrine buildings were constructed under the auspices of figures such as {{ill|Minamoto no Yoshiie|ja|源義家}}, {{ill|Minamoto no Yoritomo|ja|源頼朝}}, {{ill|Ashikaga Takauji|ja|足利尊氏}}, and {{ill|Maeda Toshiie|ja|前田利家}}. * Edo Shukkai-chō – From April 1 to 6 in the 7th year of the {{ill|Kyōhō|ja|享保}} era (1722), an opening ceremony ({{ill|Shukkai-chō|ja|出開帳}}) for the shrine's sacred object was held at the former {{ill|Mejiro Fudōin Hasedera|ja|目白不動院長谷寺}} in Edo, and on April 24 during that period, temple treasures such as hanging scrolls and documents were submitted to Edo Castle at the behest of the shogun.{{Cite web|和書|url=https://www.asahi-net.or.jp/~hm9k-ajm/musasinorekisi/gosikifudoutomusasino/mejirofudou/kitanotennjinndekaityou/kitanotennjinnsyadekaityou.htm |title=北野天神社江戸出開帳 |work=おたまじゃくし |date=2001-11-11 |publisher=Yasushima Kiichi|accessdate=2015-06}} == Shrine Grounds == Within the shrine precincts, a sanmichi (approach path) lined with {{ill|torii|ja|鳥居}} and {{ill|stone lanterns|ja|石灯籠}} is located on the west and south sides. The west side faces the old {{ill|Kamakura Kaidō|ja|鎌倉街道}}, which runs north–south, and from the south side along {{ill|Saitama-Tokyo Road 179|ja|県道179号線}}, multiple staircases and torii lead up to the haiden (worship hall). ; Shrines Within the Grounds * {{ill|Inari Shrine|ja|稲荷社}} * {{ill|Yakumo Shrine|ja|八雲社}} * {{ill|Kōkūjinja (Tokorozawa)|ja|航空神社}} – Established on September 25, Showa 12 by {{ill|Tokugawa Yoshitoshi|ja|徳川好敏}}, at the {{ill|Tokorozawa Army Airfield|ja|所沢陸軍飛行場}}. Its establishment was inspired by the plight of aviation personnel who sacrificed their lives for the development of national aviation yet were not enshrined at {{ill|Yasukuni Shrine|ja|靖国神社}}; it was thus determined that a guardian deity for national aviation should be enshrined. In Showa 13, with the founding of the {{ill|Army Air Officer Academy|ja|陸軍航空士官学校}}, the shrine was relocated from Tokorozawa to Toyooka (present-day {{ill|Iruma Base|ja|入間基地}}). On September 3, Showa 20, before the academy site was seized by the U.S. military, the shrine was re-situated within its present grounds. * {{ill|Fumiko Tenjin Shrine|ja|文子天神社}} – Enshrines Fumiko, who served as the wet nurse ({{ill|wet nurse|ja|乳母}}) of {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|ja|Sugawara no Michizane}}, known as {{ill|Tajihi Fumiko|ja|多治比文子}}. * {{ill|Kotesashi Jinja|ja|小手指神社}} – Enshrines the war dead (heroic spirits) of the Kotesashi area. ; Trees on the Grounds * {{ill|Mikotozakura|ja|尊桜}} – A cherry tree said to have been planted in front of the shrine by {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|ヤマトタケル}}, which repeatedly dies and regrows (exhibiting {{ill|Noda|ja|蘖（ひこばえ）}}). * {{ill|Dainagon Ume|ja|大納言梅}} – Planted in the 18th year of the {{ill|Tenshō Era|ja|天正}} (1590) by {{ill|Maeda Toshiie|ja|前田利家}}, currently the second generation as of 2015. It is said that Maeda Toshiie, who claimed descent from {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|ja|Sugawara no Michizane}} and used the Ume crest ({{ill|Ume Crest|ja|梅紋}}), revived the shrine by planting a single plum tree during the 【ill|Odawara Campaign|ja|小田原攻め】; his title at that time was {{ill|Dainagon|ja|大納言}}. ; Other Elements Within the Grounds * A stone monument recording the origin of the local name "Kitano" – Established on September 25, {{ill|Heisei|ja|平成}} 18 (2006). Although recent land reorganization has changed the shrine's address to Kotesashi Motomachi, the surrounding area retains the name "Kitano" as derived from this shrine. * The camp site of {{ill|Souryo Prince|ja|宗良親王}}. * A temizuya (water ablution pavilion) – Recently (in the 2010s) rebuilt with a ceiling mural depicting a {{ill|dragon|ja|龍}}. * A kaguraden (dancing hall). * A stone marker. * The sacred horse ({{ill|Shinme|ja|神馬}}). Kitano Tenjin Inari.jpg|Inari Shrine Kitano Tenjin Yagumo.jpg|Yakumo Shrine KitanoTenjin AyakoJinja.jpg|Fumiko Tenjin Shrine Kotesashi-jinja 14.jpg|Kotesashi Jinja and Kōkūjinja ; Trees and Other Features * The "Mikotozakura" cherry tree – Said to have been planted by {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|ヤマトタケル}}, this tree repeatedly dies and regrows. * The "Dainagon Ume" – Planted in the 18th year of the {{ill|Tenshō Era|ja|天正}} (1590) by {{ill|Maeda Toshiie|ja|前田利家}}, currently in its second generation as of 2015. It is named for Maeda Toshiie's former rank, {{ill|Dainagon|ja|大納言}}, and commemorates his revival of the shrine during the 【ill|Odawara Campaign|ja|小田原攻め】. * A stone monument (addressed "Kitano") – Established on September 25, {{ill|Heisei|ja|平成}} 18 (2006); it notes that the surrounding area "Kitano" derives its name from the shrine. * The camp site of {{ill|Souryo Prince|ja|宗良親王}}. * A hand-washing basin (temizuya) – Recently rebuilt (in the 2010s) with a ceiling mural depicting a dragon. * A kaguraden (dancing hall). * A power stone. * A divine horse ({{ill|Shinme|ja|神馬}}). Dainagon-ume Kitano-Tenjin-sha.jpg|Dainagon Ume Kitano Tenjin shinme.jpg|Sacred Horse == Cultural Properties == === Saitama Prefecture-designated Cultural Properties === * Tangible Cultural Property: ** Kitano Tenjin Shrine Engi (Origin Legend) (paintings) – Comprising 7 silk-colored hanging scrolls and 7 old logs.{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.city.tokorozawa.saitama.jp/iitokoro/enjoy/bunkakyoyo/bunkazai/kenshiteibunkazai/bunzai_20100510170056823.html |title=北野天神社縁起 付 旧軸木七本 |publisher=Tokorozawa City Education Committee, Cultural Property Protection Division |accessdate=2015-06}} === Tokorozawa City-designated Cultural Properties === * Tangible Cultural Property: ** The Ume Song Monument of Kitano Tenjin Shrine (a scenic spot) – Established in the 2nd year of the {{ill|Kyōwa|ja|享和}} era (1802); it is the oldest song monument in the city.{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.city.tokorozawa.saitama.jp/iitokoro/enjoy/bunkakyoyo/bunkazai/shishiteibunkazai/meisyo/bunzai_20100601150043467.html |title=尊桜の歌碑 |publisher=Tokorozawa City Education Committee, Cultural Property Protection Division |accessdate=2015-06}} ** Medieval Documents of Kitano Tenjin Shrine – A collection of 11 documents including a donation letter from the Ashikaga clan.{{Cite web|和書|url=https://www.city.tokorozawa.saitama.jp/iitokoro/enjoy/bunkakyoyo/bunkazai/shishiteibunkazai/komonjo/bunzai_20100810104554996.html |title=北野天神社中世文書 |publisher=Tokorozawa City Education Committee, Cultural Property Protection Division |accessdate=2015-06}} == Concurrent Shrines == * {{ill|Fujimori Inari Shrine (Tokorozawa)|ja|藤森稲荷神社 (所沢市)}} * {{ill|Rokusho Shrine (Tokorozawa)|ja|六所神社 (所沢市)}} * {{ill|Suwa Shrine (Tokorozawa)|ja|諏訪神社 (所沢市)}} – Located at 1-17-21 Kotesashi. Suwa Jinja Kotesashi.jpg|Suwa Shrine == List of Festivals == * New Year Festival (元旦祭, January 1) – Ritual talismans ("祈祷札") are distributed. * Hatsumōde (初詣) (January 1) * Setsubun Festival (節分祭, February 3) – Corresponds to the Ōharae at Kitano Tenjin Shrine; the "Shikinaisha Kitano Shrine Ōharae Shinpū" is distributed. * Hatsu-uma Festival (初午祭, February 11) – Held at the Inari Shrine within the precincts; "Inari Shrine Shinpū" is distributed. * Kinen-sai (祈年祭, February 27) – Also known as "Toshigoi no Matsuri"; "Kinen-sai Shinpū" is distributed. * Spring Seasonal Festival (春季例大祭, March 21) – Paired with the autumn festival, this is the most important festival at the shrine; "Kuniichi Jigisha Kaiun Shugoshinpū" is distributed. * Spring Festival (春祭, March 25) – Also called "Nibanmachi"; "Mononobe Tenjinsha Shinpū" is distributed. * Sericulture Festival (養蚕祭, April 3) – Held at the Bunkoten Shrine within the precincts; "Bunkoten Shrine Shinpū" is distributed. * Memorial Festival (慰霊祭, April 15) – Held at the Kotesashi Jinja to commemorate war dead from the Nisshin and Nichiro periods. * Yakumo Festival (八雲祭) – Held on the evening of July 14 and main festival on July 15; "Yakumo Shrine Prayer Talisman for Disaster Exorcism" is distributed. * Autumn Seasonal Festival (秋季例大祭, Late September) – Annual musical offerings and a village kagura are performed biennially. * Niiname-sai (新嘗祭, November 23) – "Niiname-sai Shinpū" is distributed.{{Cite web|和書|url=https://kitanotenjin.com/nenkangyouji.html |title=北野天神社のお祭り |publisher=Kitano Tenjin Shrine On September 3, Showa 20, before the academy site was seized by the U.S. military, the shrine was re-situated within its current grounds. * {{ill|Fumiko Tenjin Shrine|ja|文子天神社}} – Enshrines Fumiko, who served as the wet nurse ({{ill|wet nurse|ja|乳母}}) of {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|ja|Sugawara no Michizane}}, known as {{ill|Tajihi Fumiko|ja|多治比文子}}. * {{ill|Kotesashi Jinja|ja|小手指神社}} – Enshrines the war dead (heroic spirits) of the Kotesashi area. Kitano Tenjin Inari.jpg|Inari Shrine Kitano Tenjin Yagumo.jpg|Yakumo Shrine KitanoTenjin AyakoJinja.jpg|Fumiko Tenjin Shrine Kotesashi-jinja 14.jpg|Kotesashi Jinja and Kōkūjinja ; Trees on the Grounds * {{ill|Mikoto-zakura|ja|尊桜}} – A cherry tree said to have been planted in front of the shrine by {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|ヤマトタケル}}, which repeatedly dies and regrows (exhibiting {{ill|nodate|ja|蘖（ひこばえ）}}). * {{ill|Dainagon Ume|ja|大納言梅}} – Planted in the 18th year of the {{ill|Tenshō Era|ja|天正}} (1590) by {{ill|Maeda Toshiie|ja|前田利家}}, currently in its second generation as of 2015. It is named after Maeda Toshiie’s former rank, {{ill|Dainagon|ja|大納言}}, commemorating his restoration of the shrine during the {{ill|Odawara Campaign|ja|小田原攻め}}. ; Other Elements Within the Grounds * A stone monument recording the origin of the local name “Kitano” – Established on September 25, {{ill|Heisei|ja|平成}} 18 (2006); it states that the surrounding area “Kitano” derives its name from this shrine. * The campsite of {{ill|Souryo Prince|ja|宗良親王}}. * A temizuya (water ablution pavilion) – Recently rebuilt (in the 2010s) with a ceiling mural depicting a {{ill|dragon|ja|龍}}. * A kaguraden (dancing hall). * A power stone. * A divine horse ({{ill|Shinme|ja|神馬}}). Dainagon-ume Kitano-Tenjin-sha.jpg|Dainagon Ume Kitano Tenjin shinme.jpg|Sacred Horse == Cultural Properties == === Saitama Prefecture-designated Cultural Properties === * Tangible Cultural Property: ** Kitano Tenjin Shrine Engi (Origin Legend) (paintings) – Consisting of 7 silk-colored hanging scrolls and 7 old logs.{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.city.tokorozawa.saitama.jp/iitokoro/enjoy/bunkakyoyo/bunkazai/kenshiteibunkazai/bunzai_20100510170056823.html |title=Kitano Tenjin Shrine Engi, with 7 old logs |publisher=Tokorozawa City Education Committee, Cultural Property Protection Division |accessdate=2015-06}} === Tokorozawa City-designated Cultural Properties === * Tangible Cultural Property: ** The Ume Song Monument of Kitano Tenjin Shrine (a scenic spot) – Established in the 2nd year of the {{ill|Kyōwa Era|ja|享和}} (1802); it is the oldest song monument in the city.{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.city.tokorozawa.saitama.jp/iitokoro/enjoy/bunkakyoyo/bunkazai/shishiteibunkazai/meisyo/bunzai_20100601150043467.html |title=尊桜の歌碑 |publisher=Tokorozawa City Education Committee, Cultural Property Protection Division |accessdate=2015-06}} ** Medieval Documents of Kitano Tenjin Shrine – A collection of 11 documents including a donation letter from the Ashikaga clan.{{Cite web|和書|url=https://www.city.tokorozawa.saitama.jp/iitokoro/enjoy/bunkakyoyo/bunkazai/shishiteibunkazai/komonjo/bunzai_20100810104554996.html |title=Kitano Tenjin Shrine Medieval Documents |publisher=Tokorozawa City Education Committee, Cultural Property Protection Division |accessdate=2015-06}} == Concurrent Shrines == * {{ill|Fujimori Inari Shrine (Tokorozawa)|ja|藤森稲荷神社 (所沢市)}} * {{ill|Rokusho Shrine (Tokorozawa)|ja|六所神社 (所沢市)}} * {{ill|Suwa Shrine (Tokorozawa)|ja|諏訪神社 (所沢市)}} – Located at 1-17-21 Kotesashi. Suwa Jinja Kotesashi.jpg|Suwa Shrine == List of Festivals == * New Year Festival (元旦祭, January 1) – "Prayer talismans" ("祈祷札") are distributed. * Hatsumōde (初詣) (January 1) * Setsubun Festival (節分祭, February 3) – Corresponds to the Ōharae at Kitano Tenjin Shrine; the "Shikinaisha Kitano Shrine Ōharae Shinpū" is distributed. * Hatsu-uma Festival (初午祭, February 11) – Held at the Inari Shrine within the precincts; "Inari Shrine Shinpū" is distributed. * Kinen-sai (祈年祭, February 27) – Also known as "Toshigoi no Matsuri"; "Kinen-sai Shinpū" is distributed. * Spring Seasonal Festival (春季例大祭, March 21) – Paired with the autumn festival, this is the most important festival at the shrine; "Kuniichi Jigisha Kaiun Shugoshinpū" is distributed. * Spring Festival (春祭, March 25) – Also called "Nibanmachi"; "Mononobe Tenjinsha Shinpū" is distributed. * Sericulture Festival (養蚕祭, April 3) – Held at the Bunkoten Shrine within the precincts; "Bunkoten Shrine Shinpū" is distributed. * Memorial Festival (慰霊祭, April 15) – Held at Kotesashi Jinja to commemorate war dead from the Nisshin and Nichiro periods. * Yakumo Festival (八雲祭) – Held on the evening of July 14 (yo-miya) and the main festival on July 15; "Yakumo Shrine Prayer Talisman for Disaster Exorcism" is distributed. * Autumn Seasonal Festival (秋季例大祭, Late September) – Musical offerings are made annually, and a village kagura is performed every two years. * Niiname-sai (新嘗祭, November 23) – "Niiname-sai Shinpū" is distributed.{{Cite web|和書|url=https://kitanotenjin.com/nenkangyouji.html |title=Kitano Tenjin Shrine Festival|publisher=Kitano Tenjin Shrine |accessdate=2022-01-15}} == Footnotes == {{reflist}} == References == * Tokorozawa City Historical Research No.3 [https://www.city.tokorozawa.saitama.jp/iitokoro/enjoy/rekishi/sisi02.html About the Kitano Tenjin Shrine Engi Picture] (Author: Nakahara Nakatomo) == Further Reading == * {{cite book|和書|title=[[Shinpen Musashi Fudoki-kō]]|volume=巻ノ158 入間郡ノ3|chapter=Kitano-mura Tenjinsha|id={{NDLJP|764001/72}}|publisher=Geography Bureau, Ministry of Home Affairs|date=1884-6}} == External Links == {{commonscat|Kitano-Tenjin-sha, Tokorozawa}} * [https://kitanotenjin.com/ {{ill|Kitano Tenjin Shrine|ja|北野天神社}}] (Official shrine website) * {{Cite web|和書|title=Mononobe Tenjinsha, Kuniichi Jigishinja, Tenmantenjinja (Kitano Tenjin Shrine)|url=https://www.saitama-jinjacho.or.jp/shrine/8910/ |publisher=Saitama Prefectural Shrine Agency|accessdate=2018-03-12}} * {{Cite web|和書|title=Kitano Tenjin Shrine (きたのてんじんじゃ)|url=https://www.city.tokorozawa.saitama.jp/iitokoro/enjoy/kids/shokai/meisyokyuseki/kitanotenjinsya.html |publisher=Tokorozawa City|date=2008-10-31|accessdate=2017-10-15}}
