{{ill|Kensha|ja|県社|1=Prefectural Shrine|WD=Q90139226}}{{efn|Ken-sha|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kensha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} |創建 = 不明 |本殿 = |別名 = 北野天神社（総称） |例祭 = {{ill|March 21|en|March 21|WD=Q2433|lt=March 21}}（春の例大祭） |神事 = |地図 = {{Location map|Japan Saitama|label={{ill|Kitano Tenjin Shrine|ja|北野天神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kitano Tenjin Shrine|1=Kitano Tenjin Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11404275}}|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20|float=center|border=none|position=top|width=210|caption=}} {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=12|frame-align=center|frame-width=210}} }} [[File:Kitano-Tenjin-sha sandō.jpg|thumb|北野天神社 南側参道にて]] '''Kitano Tenjin Shrine''' (北野天神社, きたのてんじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto Shrine}} located in {{ill|Saitama Prefecture|en|Saitama Prefecture|WD=Q128186|lt=Saitama Prefecture}}, {{ill|Tokorozawa, Saitama|en|Tokorozawa, Saitama|WD=Q165857|lt=Tokorozawa City}}, {{ill|Kotesashi Motomachi|ja|小手指元町|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotesashi Motomachi|1=Kotesashi-Motomachi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11460790}}. It is classified as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} (two subsidiary shrines of the smaller class and one of the larger class according to the system of the {{ill|Engishiki Shinmeichō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Shinmeichō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}), with its former Ranking under the modern shrine Ranking system being that of a {{ill|Kensha|ja|県社|1=Prefectural Shrine|WD=Q90139226}}{{efn|Ken-sha|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kensha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}. The registered name of the religious corporation is '''{{ill|Mononobe Tenjinsha|ja|物部天神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mononobe Tenjinsha|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}・{{ill|Kuniichi Jigishinja|ja|國渭地祇神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuniichi Jigishinja|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 国渭地祇社|1=kuniichinoyashiro|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q55523456}}・{{ill|Tenmantenjinja|ja|天満天神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmantenjinja|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}'''; "Kitano Tenjin Shrine" is a collective term for these shrines.{{Cite web|and=|url=http://www.city.tokorozawa.saitama.jp/iitokoro/enjoy/kids/shokai/meisyokyuseki/kitanotenjinsya.html |title=北野天神社（きたのてんじんしゃ）（北野） |date=2008-10-31 |publisher=Tokorozawa City Education Committee, Cultural Property Protection Division |accessdate=2015-06}} == {{nihongo|Worshipped deities|祭神|Saijin}} == * {{ill|Mononobe Tenjinsha|ja|物部天神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mononobe Tenjinsha|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (もののべてんじんじゃ): Enshrines {{ill|Nigihayahi|ja|ニギハヤヒ|lt=Kushitama Nigi Hayahito|lt_ja=饒速日命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nigihayahi|qq=}}, designated as the subsidiary shrine "Mononobe Tenjinsha" within the system; it is enshrined together with {{ill|Izumo Ihabishi Shrine|ja|出雲伊波比神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo Ihabishi Shrine|1=Izumoiwai Shrine, Moroyama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q30933323}}. * {{ill|Kuniichi Jigishinja|ja|国渭地祇神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuniichi Jigishinja|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 国渭地祇社|1=kuniichinoyashiro|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q55523456}} (くにいちぎじんじゃ): Enshrines {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en|Ōkuninushi|WD=Q276944|lt=Yachihoko no Mikoto}}, designated as the subsidiary shrine "Kuniichi Jigisha" ({{ill|Izumo Ihabishi Shrine|ja|出雲伊波比神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo Ihabishi Shrine|1=Izumoiwai Shrine, Moroyama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q30933323}} is enshrined together). * {{ill|Tenmantenjinja|ja|天満天神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmantenjinja|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (てんまんてんじんじゃ): Enshrines {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|1=Sugawara no Michizane|2=ja|3=菅原道真|ja|Sugawara no Michizane|1=Sugawara no Michizane|2=ja|3=菅原道真|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugawara no Michizane|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q382005}}. === 合祀 === * {{ill|Prince Munenaga|en|Prince Munenaga|WD=Q541057|lt=Souryo Prince}} (むねよししんのう) * {{ill|Kotesashi Myojin|ja|小手指明神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotesashi Myojin|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} * {{ill|Ame no Hohi|en|Ame no Hohi|WD=Q10940685|lt=Amenohohi no Mikoto}} * {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|en|Emperor Ōjin|WD=Q317997|lt=Emperor Ojin}} * {{ill|Yamato Takeru|en|Yamato Takeru|WD=Q461258|lt=Prince Yamato Takeru}} * {{ill|Ukanomitama|en|Ukanomitama|WD=Q3080728|lt=Ukano Mitama no Mikoto}} == History == According to shrine tradition, it is said that {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|日本武尊|1=Yamato Takeru|lt=Prince Yamato Takeru|3=ヤマトタケル|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Takeru|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Takeru|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ヤマトタケル|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q461258}} enshrined this site during his eastern expedition. In the {{ill|Edo period|en|Edo period|WD=Q184963|lt=Edo period}}, the Edo Bakufu granted {{ill|Shuinjo|ja|朱印状|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shuinjo|1=shuinjō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11093673}} to the shrine. * The Mononobe Tenjinsha was the tutelary shrine of the Mononobe clan (see {{ill|Mujashi Kunizukuri|ja|无邪志国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mujashi Kunizukuri|1=Musashi no Kuni no Miyatsuko|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11504612}} for the family) and continues to enshrine their ancestral deity, {{ill|Nigihayahi|ja|ニギハヤヒ|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nigihayahi|qq=}}. * As a Tenjin Shrine, it was first enshrined by {{ill|Sugawara no Shūsei|ja|菅原修成|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugawara no Shūsei|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, a 5th-generation descendant of {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|1=Sugawara no Michizane|2=ja|3=菅原道真|ja|Sugawara no Michizane|1=Sugawara no Michizane|2=ja|3=菅原道真|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugawara no Michizane|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q382005}}, in the first year of the {{ill|Chōtoku|en|Chōtoku|WD=Q1327213|lt=Chōtoku}} era (995) as a guardian in his capacity as {{ill|Musashi-no-Mori|ja|武蔵守|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Musashi-no-Mori|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 武蔵国司|1=musashikokushi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11546337}}, sent from Kyoto's {{ill|Kitano Tenmangū|en|Kitano Tenmangū|WD=Q662176|lt=Kitano Shrine}}. Subsequently, the shrine buildings were constructed under the auspices of figures such as {{ill|Minamoto no Yoshiie|en|Minamoto no Yoshiie|WD=Q32613|lt=Minamoto no Yoshiie}}, {{ill|Minamoto no Yoritomo|en|Minamoto no Yoritomo|WD=Q242800|lt=Minamoto no Yoritomo}}, {{ill|Ashikaga Takauji|en|Ashikaga Takauji|WD=Q297107|lt=Ashikaga Takauji}}, and {{ill|Maeda Toshiie|en|Maeda Toshiie|WD=Q1196817|lt=Maeda Toshiie}}. * Edo Shukkai-chō – From April 1 to 6 in the 7th year of the {{ill|Kyōhō|en|Kyōhō|WD=Q1145048|lt=Kyōhō}} era (1722), an opening ceremony ({{ill|Shukkai-chō|ja|出開帳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shukkai-chō|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 開帳|1=kaichō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q6347588}}) for the shrine's sacred object was held at the former {{ill|Mejiro Fudōin Hasedera|ja|目白不動院長谷寺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mejiro Fudōin Hasedera|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} in Edo, and on April 24 during that period, temple treasures such as hanging scrolls and documents were submitted to Edo Castle at the behest of the shogun.{{Cite web|和書|url=https://www.asahi-net.or.jp/~hm9k-ajm/musasinorekisi/gosikifudoutomusasino/mejirofudou/kitanotennjinndekaityou/kitanotennjinnsyadekaityou.htm |title=北野天神社江戸出開帳 |work=おたまじゃくし |date=2001-11-11 |publisher=Yasushima Kiichi|accessdate=2015-06}} == Shrine Grounds == Within the shrine precincts, a sanmichi (approach path) lined with {{ill|Torii|en|Torii|WD=Q234731|lt=torii}} and {{ill|stone lanterns|ja|石灯籠|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/stone lanterns|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 灯籠|1=Stone lantern|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q12012294}} is located on the west and south sides. The west side faces the old {{ill|Kamakura Kaidō|en|Kamakura Kaidō|WD=Q2389309|lt=Kamakura Kaidō}}, which runs north–south, and from the south side along {{ill|Saitama-Tokyo Road 179|ja|県道179号線|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saitama-Tokyo Road 179|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, multiple staircases and torii lead up to the haiden (worship hall). ; Shrines Within the Grounds * {{ill|Inari Shrine|ja|稲荷社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inari Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 稲荷神社|1=Inari shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q514480}} * {{ill|Yakumo Shrine|ja|八雲社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yakumo Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} * {{ill|Kōkūjinja (Tokorozawa)|ja|航空神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōkūjinja (Tokorozawa)|1=Aviation Shrines|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q30319396}} – Established on September 25, Showa 12 by {{ill|Yoshitoshi Tokugawa|en|Yoshitoshi Tokugawa|WD=Q5694703|lt=Tokugawa Yoshitoshi}}, at the {{ill|Tokorozawa Army Airfield|ja|所沢陸軍飛行場|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokorozawa Army Airfield|1=Tokorozawa Airfield|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11658682}}. Its establishment was inspired by the plight of aviation personnel who sacrificed their lives for the development of national aviation yet were not enshrined at {{ill|Yasukuni Shrine|en|Yasukuni Shrine|WD=Q242803|lt=Yasukuni Shrine}}; it was thus determined that a guardian deity for national aviation should be enshrined. In Showa 13, with the founding of the {{ill|Imperial Japanese Army Air Academy|en|Imperial Japanese Army Air Academy|WD=Q2822344|lt=Army Air Officer Academy}}, the shrine was relocated from Tokorozawa to Toyooka (present-day {{ill|Iruma Air Base|en|Iruma Air Base|WD=Q3015843|lt=Iruma Base}}). On September 3, Showa 20, before the academy site was seized by the U.S. military, the shrine was re-situated within its present grounds. * {{ill|Fumiko Tenjin Shrine|ja|文子天神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fumiko Tenjin Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|WD=Q135579708}} – Enshrines Fumiko, who served as the wet nurse ({{ill|Wet nurse|en|Wet nurse|WD=Q472898|lt=wet nurse}}) of {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|1=Sugawara no Michizane|2=ja|3=菅原道真|ja|Sugawara no Michizane|1=Sugawara no Michizane|2=ja|3=菅原道真|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugawara no Michizane|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q382005}}, known as {{ill|Tajihi Fumiko|ja|多治比文子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tajihi Fumiko|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. * {{ill|Kotesashi Jinja|ja|小手指神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotesashi Jinja|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|WD=Q135579709}} – Enshrines the war dead (heroic spirits) of the Kotesashi area. ; Trees on the Grounds * {{ill|Mikotozakura|ja|尊桜|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mikotozakura|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} – A cherry tree said to have been planted in front of the shrine by {{ill|Yamato Takeru|en|Yamato Takeru|WD=Q461258|lt=Yamato Takeru}}, which repeatedly dies and regrows (exhibiting {{ill|Noda|ja|蘖（ひこばえ）|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Noda|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}). * {{ill|Dainagon Ume|ja|大納言梅|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dainagon Ume|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} – Planted in the 18th year of the {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|en|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|WD=Q1145058|lt=Tenshō Era}} (1590) by {{ill|Maeda Toshiie|en|Maeda Toshiie|WD=Q1196817|lt=Maeda Toshiie}}, currently the second generation as of 2015. It is said that Maeda Toshiie, who claimed descent from {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|1=Sugawara no Michizane|2=ja|3=菅原道真|ja|Sugawara no Michizane|1=Sugawara no Michizane|2=ja|3=菅原道真|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugawara no Michizane|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q382005}} and used the Ume crest ({{ill|Ume Crest|ja|梅紋|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ume Crest|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ウメ|1=Prunus mume|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q157763}}), revived the shrine by planting a single plum tree during the 【ill|Odawara Campaign|ja|小田原攻め】; his title at that time was {{ill|Dainagon|en|Dainagon|WD=Q1354706|lt=Dainagon}}. ; Other Elements Within the Grounds * A stone monument recording the origin of the local name "Kitano" – Established on September 25, {{ill|Heisei era|en|Heisei era|WD=Q234510|lt=Heisei}} 18 (2006). Although recent land reorganization has changed the shrine's address to Kotesashi Motomachi, the surrounding area retains the name "Kitano" as derived from this shrine. * The camp site of {{ill|Prince Munenaga|en|Prince Munenaga|WD=Q541057|lt=Souryo Prince}}. * A temizuya (water ablution pavilion) – Recently (in the 2010s) rebuilt with a ceiling mural depicting a {{ill|dragon|ja|龍|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/dragon|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 竜|1=dragon|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q7559}}. * A kaguraden (dancing hall). * A stone marker. * The sacred horse ({{ill|Shinme|ja|神馬|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinme|qq=}}). Kitano Tenjin Inari.jpg|Inari Shrine Kitano Tenjin Yagumo.jpg|Yakumo Shrine KitanoTenjin AyakoJinja.jpg|Fumiko Tenjin Shrine Kotesashi-jinja 14.jpg|Kotesashi Jinja and Kōkūjinja ; Trees and Other Features * The "Mikotozakura" cherry tree – Said to have been planted by {{ill|Yamato Takeru|en|Yamato Takeru|WD=Q461258|lt=Yamato Takeru}}, this tree repeatedly dies and regrows. * The "Dainagon Ume" – Planted in the 18th year of the {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|en|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|WD=Q1145058|lt=Tenshō Era}} (1590) by {{ill|Maeda Toshiie|en|Maeda Toshiie|WD=Q1196817|lt=Maeda Toshiie}}, currently in its second generation as of 2015. It is named for Maeda Toshiie's former Rank, {{ill|Dainagon|en|Dainagon|WD=Q1354706|lt=Dainagon}}, and commemorates his revival of the shrine during the 【ill|Odawara Campaign|ja|小田原攻め】. * A stone monument (addressed "Kitano") – Established on September 25, {{ill|Heisei era|en|Heisei era|WD=Q234510|lt=Heisei}} 18 (2006); it notes that the surrounding area "Kitano" derives its name from the shrine. * The camp site of {{ill|Prince Munenaga|en|Prince Munenaga|WD=Q541057|lt=Souryo Prince}}. * A hand-washing basin (temizuya) – Recently rebuilt (in the 2010s) with a ceiling mural depicting a dragon. * A kaguraden (dancing hall). * A power stone. * A divine horse ({{ill|Shinme|ja|神馬|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinme|qq=}}). Dainagon-ume Kitano-Tenjin-sha.jpg|Dainagon Ume Kitano Tenjin shinme.jpg|Sacred Horse == Cultural Properties == === Saitama Prefecture-designated Cultural Properties === * Tangible Cultural Property: ** Kitano Tenjin Shrine Engi (Origin Legend) (paintings) – Comprising 7 silk-colored hanging scrolls and 7 old logs.{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.city.tokorozawa.saitama.jp/iitokoro/enjoy/bunkakyoyo/bunkazai/kenshiteibunkazai/bunzai_20100510170056823.html |title=北野天神社縁起 付 旧軸木七本 |publisher=Tokorozawa City Education Committee, Cultural Property Protection Division |accessdate=2015-06}} === Tokorozawa City-designated Cultural Properties === * Tangible Cultural Property: ** The Ume Song Monument of Kitano Tenjin Shrine (a scenic spot) – Established in the 2nd year of the {{ill|Kyōwa|en|Kyōwa|WD=Q960763|lt=Kyōwa}} era (1802); it is the oldest song monument in the city.{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.city.tokorozawa.saitama.jp/iitokoro/enjoy/bunkakyoyo/bunkazai/shishiteibunkazai/meisyo/bunzai_20100601150043467.html |title=尊桜の歌碑 |publisher=Tokorozawa City Education Committee, Cultural Property Protection Division |accessdate=2015-06}} ** Medieval Documents of Kitano Tenjin Shrine – A collection of 11 documents including a donation letter from the Ashikaga clan.{{Cite web|和書|url=https://www.city.tokorozawa.saitama.jp/iitokoro/enjoy/bunkakyoyo/bunkazai/shishiteibunkazai/komonjo/bunzai_20100810104554996.html |title=北野天神社中世文書 |publisher=Tokorozawa City Education Committee, Cultural Property Protection Division |accessdate=2015-06}} == Concurrent Shrines == * {{ill|Fujimori Inari Shrine (Tokorozawa)|ja|藤森稲荷神社 (所沢市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujimori Inari Shrine (Tokorozawa)|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|WD=Q135579710}} * {{ill|Rokusho Shrine (Tokorozawa)|ja|六所神社 (所沢市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rokusho Shrine (Tokorozawa)|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 上新井|1=Kamiarai|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11359054}} * {{ill|Suwa Shrine (Tokorozawa)|ja|諏訪神社 (所沢市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suwa Shrine (Tokorozawa)|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} – Located at 1-17-21 Kotesashi. Suwa Jinja Kotesashi.jpg|Suwa Shrine == List of Festivals == * New Year Festival (元旦祭, January 1) – Ritual talismans ("祈祷札") are distributed. * Hatsumōde (初詣) (January 1) * Setsubun Festival (節分祭, February 3) – Corresponds to the Ōharae at Kitano Tenjin Shrine; the "Shikinaisha Kitano Shrine Ōharae Shinpū" is distributed. * Hatsu-uma Festival (初午祭, February 11) – Held at the Inari Shrine within the precincts; "Inari Shrine Shinpū" is distributed. * Kinen-sai (祈年祭, February 27) – Also known as "Toshigoi no Matsuri"; "Kinen-sai Shinpū" is distributed. * Spring Seasonal Festival (春季例大祭, March 21) – Paired with the autumn festival, this is the most important festival at the shrine; "Kuniichi Jigisha Kaiun Shugoshinpū" is distributed. * Spring Festival (春祭, March 25) – Also called "Nibanmachi"; "Mononobe Tenjinsha Shinpū" is distributed. * Sericulture Festival (養蚕祭, April 3) – Held at the Bunkoten Shrine within the precincts; "Bunkoten Shrine Shinpū" is distributed. * Memorial Festival (慰霊祭, April 15) – Held at the Kotesashi Jinja to commemorate war dead from the Nisshin and Nichiro periods. * Yakumo Festival (八雲祭) – Held on the evening of July 14 and main festival on July 15; "Yakumo Shrine Prayer Talisman for Disaster Exorcism" is distributed. * Autumn Seasonal Festival (秋季例大祭, Late September) – Annual musical offerings and a village kagura are performed biennially. * Niiname-sai (新嘗祭, November 23) – "Niiname-sai Shinpū" is distributed.{{Cite web|和書|url=https://kitanotenjin.com/nenkangyouji.html |title=北野天神社のお祭り |publisher=Kitano Tenjin Shrine |accessdate=2022-01-15}} == Footnotes == {{reflist}} == References == * Tokorozawa City Historical Research No.3 [https://www.city.tokorozawa.saitama.jp/iitokoro/enjoy/rekishi/sisi02.html About the Kitano Tenjin Shrine Engi Picture] (Author: Nakahara Nakatomo) == Further Reading == * {{cite book|和書|title=[[Shinpen Musashi Fudoki-kō]]|volume=巻ノ158 入間郡ノ3|chapter=Kitano-mura Tenjinsha|id={{NDLJP|764001/72}}|publisher=Geography Bureau, Ministry of Home Affairs|date=1884-6}} == External Links == {{commonscat|Kitano-Tenjin-sha, Tokorozawa}} * [https://kitanotenjin.com/] (Official shrine website) * {{Cite web|和書|title=Mononobe Tenjinsha, Kuniichi Jigishinja, Tenmantenjinja (Kitano Tenjin Shrine)|url=https://www.saitama-jinjacho.or.jp/shrine/8910/ |publisher=Saitama Prefectural Shrine Agency|accessdate=2018-03-12}} * {{Cite web|和書|title=Kitano Tenjin Shrine (きたのてんじんじゃ)|url=https://www.city.tokorozawa.saitama.jp/iitokoro/enjoy/kids/shokai/meisyokyuseki/kitanotenjinsya.html |publisher=Tokorozawa City|date=2008-10-31|accessdate=2017-10-15}} {{translated page|ja|北野天神社 (所沢市)|version=101465493|comment=Imported full ja history}} [[ceb:Kitano Tenjinsha (Tokorozawa)]] [[ja:北野天神社]] {{Commons category|Kitano-Tenjin-sha, Tokorozawa}} [[ja:北野天神社 (所沢市)]] {{Shinja |名称 = {{ill|Mononobe Tenjin Shrine|ja|物部天神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mononobe Tenjin Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}・{{ill|Kuniichi Jigishinja|ja|国渭地祇神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuniichi Jigishinja|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 国渭地祇社|1=kuniichinoyashiro|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q55523456}}

tradition, it is said that {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|日本武尊|1=Yamato Takeru|lt=Prince Yamato Takeru|3=ヤマトタケル|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Takeru|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Takeru|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ヤマトタケル|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q461258}} enshrined this site during his eastern expedition. In the Edo period, the Edo Bakufu granted {{ill|Shuinjo|ja|朱印状|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shuinjo|1=shuinjō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11093673}} to the shrine. * The Mononobe Tenjin Shrine served as the tutelary shrine of the Mononobe clan (see {{ill|Mujashi Kunizukuri|ja|无邪志国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mujashi Kunizukuri|1=Musashi no Kuni no Miyatsuko|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11504612}} for details on the clan) and still enshrines their ancestral deity, {{ill|Nigihayahi|ja|ニギハヤヒ|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nigihayahi|qq=}}. * As a Tenjin shrine, it was established in the first year of the {{ill|Chōtoku|en|Chōtoku|WD=Q1327213|lt=Chōtoku}} era (995) when {{ill|Sugawara no Shūsei|ja|菅原修成|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugawara no Shūsei|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, a fifth-generation descendant of {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|1=Sugawara no Michizane|2=ja|3=菅原道真|ja|Sugawara no Michizane|1=Sugawara no Michizane|2=ja|3=菅原道真|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugawara no Michizane|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q382005}}, was commissioned as {{ill|Musashi-no-Mori|ja|武蔵守|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Musashi-no-Mori|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 武蔵国司|1=musashikokushi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11546337}} from Kyoto’s {{ill|Kitano Tenmangū|en|Kitano Tenmangū|WD=Q662176|lt=Kitano Tenmangu}}; thereafter, the shrine buildings were constructed under the auspices of figures such as {{ill|Minamoto no Yoshiie|en|Minamoto no Yoshiie|WD=Q32613|lt=Minamoto no Yoshiie}}, {{ill|Minamoto no Yoritomo|en|Minamoto no Yoritomo|WD=Q242800|lt=Minamoto no Yoritomo}}, {{ill|Ashikaga Takauji|en|Ashikaga Takauji|WD=Q297107|lt=Ashikaga Takauji}}, and {{ill|Maeda Toshiie|en|Maeda Toshiie|WD=Q1196817|lt=Maeda Toshiie}}. * Edo Shukkai-chō – From April 1 to 6 in the 7th year of the {{ill|Kyōhō|en|Kyōhō|WD=Q1145048|lt=Kyōhō}} era (1722), an opening ceremony for the shrine’s sacred object was held at the former {{ill|Mejiro Fudōin Hasedera|ja|目白不動院長谷寺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mejiro Fudōin Hasedera|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} in Edo, and on April 24 during that period, shrine treasures such as hanging scrolls and documents were submitted to Edo Castle at the shogun’s behest.{{Cite web|和書|url=https://www.asahi-net.or.jp/~hm9k-ajm/musasinorekisi/gosikifudoutomusasino/mejirofudou/kitanotennjinndekaityou/kitanotennjinnsyadekaityou.htm |title=北野天神社江戸出開帳 |work=おたまじゃくし |date=2001-11-11 |publisher=Yasushima Kiichi|accessdate=2015-06}} == Shrine Grounds == The shrine grounds feature an approach path lined with {{ill|Torii|en|Torii|WD=Q234731|lt=torii}} and {{ill|stone lanterns|ja|石灯籠|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/stone lanterns|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 灯籠|1=Stone lantern|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q12012294}} on the west and south sides. The west side faces the old {{ill|Kamakura Kaidō|en|Kamakura Kaidō|WD=Q2389309|lt=Kamakura Kaidō}}, which runs north–south, and from the south side along {{ill|Saitama-Tokyo Road 179|ja|県道179号線|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saitama-Tokyo Road 179|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, multiple staircases and torii lead up to the area in front of the haiden (worship hall). ; Shrines Within the Grounds * {{ill|Inari Shrine|ja|稲荷社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inari Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 稲荷神社|1=Inari shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q514480}} * {{ill|Yakumo Shrine|ja|八雲社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yakumo Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} * {{ill|Kōkūjinja (Tokorozawa)|ja|航空神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōkūjinja (Tokorozawa)|1=Aviation Shrines|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q30319396}} – Established on September 25, Showa 12 by {{ill|Yoshitoshi Tokugawa|en|Yoshitoshi Tokugawa|WD=Q5694703|lt=Tokugawa Yoshitoshi}} at the {{ill|Tokorozawa Army Airfield|ja|所沢陸軍飛行場|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokorozawa Army Airfield|1=Tokorozawa Airfield|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11658682}}. Its establishment was prompted by the plight of aviation personnel who sacrificed their lives for the development of national aviation yet were not enshrined at {{ill|Yasukuni Shrine|en|Yasukuni Shrine|WD=Q242803|lt=Yasukuni Shrine}}. In Showa 13, with the founding of the {{ill|Imperial Japanese Army Air Academy|en|Imperial Japanese Army Air Academy|WD=Q2822344|lt=Army Air Officer Academy}}, the shrine was relocated from Tokorozawa to Toyooka (present-day {{ill|Iruma Air Base|en|Iruma Air Base|WD=Q3015843|lt=Iruma Base}}). On September 3, Showa 20, before the academy site was seized by the U.S. military, the shrine was re-situated within its current grounds. * {{ill|Fumiko Tenjin Shrine|ja|文子天神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fumiko Tenjin Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|WD=Q135579708}} – Enshrines Fumiko, who served as the wet nurse ({{ill|Wet nurse|en|Wet nurse|WD=Q472898|lt=wet nurse}}) of {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|1=Sugawara no Michizane|2=ja|3=菅原道真|ja|Sugawara no Michizane|1=Sugawara no Michizane|2=ja|3=菅原道真|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugawara no Michizane|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q382005}}, known as {{ill|Tajihi Fumiko|ja|多治比文子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tajihi Fumiko|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. * {{ill|Kotesashi Jinja|ja|小手指神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotesashi Jinja|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|WD=Q135579709}} – Enshrines the war dead (heroic spirits) of the Kotesashi area. Kitano Tenjin Inari.jpg|Inari Shrine Kitano Tenjin Yagumo.jpg|Yakumo Shrine KitanoTenjin AyakoJinja.jpg|Fumiko Tenjin Shrine Kotesashi-jinja 14.jpg|Kotesashi Jinja and Kōkūjinja ; Trees on the Grounds * {{ill|Mikoto-zakura|ja|尊桜|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mikoto-zakura|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} – A cherry tree said to have been planted in front of the shrine by {{ill|Yamato Takeru|en|Yamato Takeru|WD=Q461258|lt=Yamato Takeru}}, which repeatedly dies and regrows (exhibiting {{ill|nodate|ja|蘖（ひこばえ）|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/nodate|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}). * {{ill|Dainagon Ume|ja|大納言梅|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dainagon Ume|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} – Planted in the 18th year of the {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|en|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|WD=Q1145058|lt=Tenshō Era}} (1590) by {{ill|Maeda Toshiie|en|Maeda Toshiie|WD=Q1196817|lt=Maeda Toshiie}}, currently in its second generation as of 2015. It is named after Maeda Toshiie’s former Rank, {{ill|Dainagon|en|Dainagon|WD=Q1354706|lt=Dainagon}}, commemorating his restoration of the shrine during the {{ill|Siege of Odawara|en|Siege of Odawara|WD=Q4372123|lt=Odawara Campaign}}. ; Other Elements Within the Grounds * A stone monument recording the origin of the local name “Kitano” – Established on September 25, {{ill|Heisei era|en|Heisei era|WD=Q234510|lt=Heisei}} 18 (2006); it states that the surrounding area “Kitano” derives its name from this shrine. * The campsite of {{ill|Prince Munenaga|en|Prince Munenaga|WD=Q541057|lt=Souryo Prince}}. * A temizuya (water ablution pavilion) – Recently rebuilt (in the 2010s) with a ceiling mural depicting a {{ill|dragon|ja|龍|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/dragon|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 竜|1=dragon|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q7559}}. * A kaguraden (dancing hall). * A power stone. * A divine horse ({{ill|Shinme|ja|神馬|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinme|qq=}}). Dainagon-ume Kitano-Tenjin-sha.jpg|Dainagon Ume Kitano Tenjin shinme.jpg|Sacred Horse == Cultural Properties == === Saitama Prefecture-designated Cultural Properties === * Tangible Cultural Property: ** Kitano Tenjin Shrine Engi (Origin Legend) (paintings) – Consisting of 7 silk-colored hanging scrolls and 7 old logs.{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.city.tokorozawa.saitama.jp/iitokoro/enjoy/bunkakyoyo/bunkazai/kenshiteibunkazai/bunzai_20100510170056823.html |title=Kitano Tenjin Shrine Engi, with 7 old logs |publisher=Tokorozawa City Education Committee, Cultural Property Protection Division |accessdate=2015-06}} === Tokorozawa City-designated Cultural Properties === * Tangible Cultural Property: ** The Ume Song Monument of Kitano Tenjin Shrine (a scenic spot) – Established in the 2nd year of the {{ill|Kyōwa|en|Kyōwa|WD=Q960763|lt=Kyōwa Era}} (1802); it is the oldest song monument in the city.{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.city.tokorozawa.saitama.jp/iitokoro/enjoy/bunkakyoyo/bunkazai/shishiteibunkazai/meisyo/bunzai_20100601150043467.html |title=尊桜の歌碑 |publisher=Tokorozawa City Education Committee, Cultural Property Protection Division |accessdate=2015-06}} ** Medieval Documents of Kitano Tenjin Shrine – A collection of 11 documents including a donation letter from the Ashikaga clan.{{Cite web|和書|url=https://www.city.tokorozawa.saitama.jp/iitokoro/enjoy/bunkakyoyo/bunkazai/shishiteibunkazai/komonjo/bunzai_20100810104554996.html |title=Kitano Tenjin Shrine Medieval Documents |publisher=Tokorozawa City Education Committee, Cultural Property Protection Division |accessdate=2015-06}} == Concurrent Shrines == * {{ill|Fujimori Inari Shrine (Tokorozawa)|ja|藤森稲荷神社 (所沢市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujimori Inari Shrine (Tokorozawa)|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|WD=Q135579710}} * {{ill|Rokusho Shrine (Tokorozawa)|ja|六所神社 (所沢市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rokusho Shrine (Tokorozawa)|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 上新井|1=Kamiarai|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11359054}} * {{ill|Suwa Shrine (Tokorozawa)|ja|諏訪神社 (所沢市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suwa Shrine (Tokorozawa)|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} – Located at 1-17-21 Kotesashi. Suwa Jinja Kotesashi.jpg|Suwa Shrine == List of Festivals == * New Year Festival (元旦祭, January 1) – "Prayer talismans" ("祈祷札") are distributed. * Hatsumōde (初詣) (January 1) * Setsubun Festival (節分祭, February 3) – Corresponds to the Ōharae at Kitano Tenjin Shrine; the "Shikinaisha Kitano Shrine Ōharae Shinpū" is distributed. * Hatsu-uma Festival (初午祭, February 11) – Held at the Inari Shrine within the precincts; "Inari Shrine Shinpū" is distributed. * Kinen-sai (祈年祭, February 27) – Also known as "Toshigoi no Matsuri"; "Kinen-sai Shinpū" is distributed. * Spring Seasonal Festival (春季例大祭, March 21) – Paired with the autumn festival, this is the most important festival at the shrine; "Kuniichi Jigisha Kaiun Shugoshinpū" is distributed. * Spring Festival (春祭, March 25) – Also called "Nibanmachi"; "Mononobe Tenjinsha Shinpū" is distributed. * Sericulture Festival (養蚕祭, April 3) – Held at the Bunkoten Shrine within the precincts; "Bunkoten Shrine Shinpū" is distributed. * Memorial Festival (慰霊祭, April 15) – Held at Kotesashi Jinja to commemorate war dead from the Nisshin and Nichiro periods. * Yakumo Festival (八雲祭) – Held on the evening of July 14 (yo-miya) and the main festival on July 15; "Yakumo Shrine Prayer Talisman for Disaster Exorcism" is distributed. * Autumn Seasonal Festival (秋季例大祭, Late September) – Musical offerings are made annually, and a village kagura is performed every two years. * Niiname-sai (新嘗祭, November 23) – "Niiname-sai Shinpū" is distributed.{{Cite web|和書|url=https://kitanotenjin.com/nenkangyouji.html |title=Kitano Tenjin Shrine Festival|publisher=Kitano Tenjin Shrine |accessdate=2022-01-15}} == Footnotes == {{reflist}} == References == * Tokorozawa City Historical Research No.3 [https://www.city.tokorozawa.saitama.jp/iitokoro/enjoy/rekishi/sisi02.html About the Kitano Tenjin Shrine Engi Picture] (Author: Nakahara Nakatomo) == Further Reading == * {{cite book|和書|title=[[Shinpen Musashi Fudoki-kō]]|volume=巻ノ158 入間郡ノ3|chapter=Kitano-mura Tenjinsha|id={{NDLJP|764001/72}}|publisher=Geography Bureau, Ministry of Home Affairs|date=1884-6}} == External Links == {{commonscat|Kitano-Tenjin-sha, Tokorozawa}} * [https://kitanotenjin.com/ {{bad link|These are causing so much issues|Kitano Tenjin Shrine|ja|北野天神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kitano Tenjin Shrine|qq=}}] (Official shrine website) * {{Cite web|和書|title=Mononobe Tenjinsha, Kuniichi Jigishinja, Tenmantenjinja (Kitano Tenjin Shrine)|url=https://www.saitama-jinjacho.or.jp/shrine/8910/ |publisher=Saitama Prefectural Shrine Agency|accessdate=2018-03-12}} * {{Cite web|和書|title=Kitano Tenjin Shrine (きたのてんじんじゃ)|url=https://www.city.tokorozawa.saitama.jp/iitokoro/enjoy/kids/shokai/meisyokyuseki/kitanotenjinsya.html |publisher=Tokorozawa City|date=2008-10-31|accessdate=2017-10-15}} {{translated 拝殿 |所在地 = {{ill|Saitama Prefecture|en|Saitama Prefecture|WD=Q128186|lt=Saitama Prefecture}}{{ill|Tokorozawa, Saitama|en|Tokorozawa, Saitama|WD=Q165857|lt=Tokorozawa City}}{{ill|Kotesashi Motomachi|ja|小手指元町|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotesashi Motomachi|1=Kotesashi-Motomachi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11460790}}3-28-44 |位置 = {{Coord|35|47|26.0|N|139|25|43.3|E|region:JP-11_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name={{ill|Kitano Tenjin Shrine|ja|北野天神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kitano Tenjin Shrine|1=Kitano Tenjin Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11404275}}}} |祭神 = {{ill|Nigihayahi|ja|ニギハヤヒ|lt=Kushitama Nigi Hayahito|lt_ja=櫛玉饒速日命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nigihayahi|qq=}}
{{ill|Ōkuninushi|en|Ōkuninushi|WD=Q276944|lt=Yachihoko no Mikoto}}
{{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|1=Sugawara no Michizane|2=ja|3=菅原道真|ja|Sugawara no Michizane|1=Sugawara no Michizane|2=ja|3=菅原道真|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugawara no Michizane|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q382005}} |社格 = {{ill|Engishiki Shinmeichō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|lt=Shikinaisha|lt_ja=式内社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Shinmeichō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}（小2・小1{{ill|Ronsha|ja|論社|1=candidate shrines|2=ja|3=論社|lt=candidate|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ronsha|13=User:Immanuelle/candidate shrines|1=Engishiki_Jinmyōchō#Ronsha|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki_Jinmyocho|lt=Ronsha}}}}）
{{ill|Kensha|ja|県社|1=Prefectural Shrine|WD=Q90139226}}{{efn|Ken-sha|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kensha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} |創建 = 不明 |本殿 = |別名 = 北野天神社（総称） |例祭 = {{ill|March 21|en|March 21|WD=Q2433|lt=March 21}}（春の例大祭） |神事 = |地図 = {{Location map|Japan Saitama|label={{ill|Kitano Tenjin Shrine|ja|北野天神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kitano Tenjin Shrine|1=Kitano Tenjin Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11404275}}|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20|float=center|border=none|position=top|width=210|caption=}} {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=12|frame-align=center|frame-width=210}} }} [[File:Kitano-Tenjin-sha sandō.jpg|thumb|北野天神社 南側参道にて]] '''Kitano Tenjin Shrine''' (北野天神社, きたのてんじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto Shrine}} located in {{ill|Saitama Prefecture|en|Saitama Prefecture|WD=Q128186|lt=Saitama Prefecture}}, {{ill|Tokorozawa, Saitama|en|Tokorozawa, Saitama|WD=Q165857|lt=Tokorozawa City}}, {{ill|Kotesashi Motomachi|ja|小手指元町|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotesashi Motomachi|1=Kotesashi-Motomachi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11460790}}. It is classified as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} (two subsidiary shrines of the smaller class and one of the larger class according to the system of the {{ill|Engishiki Shinmeichō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Shinmeichō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}), with its former Ranking under the modern shrine Ranking system being that of a {{ill|Kensha|ja|県社|1=Prefectural Shrine|WD=Q90139226}}{{efn|Ken-sha|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kensha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}. The registered name of the religious corporation is '''{{ill|Mononobe Tenjinsha|ja|物部天神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mononobe Tenjinsha|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}・{{ill|Kuniichi Jigishinja|ja|國渭地祇神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuniichi Jigishinja|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 国渭地祇社|1=kuniichinoyashiro|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q55523456}}・{{ill|Tenmantenjinja|ja|天満天神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmantenjinja|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}'''; "Kitano Tenjin Shrine" is a collective term for these shrines.{{Cite web|and=|url=http://www.city.tokorozawa.saitama.jp/iitokoro/enjoy/kids/shokai/meisyokyuseki/kitanotenjinsya.html |title=北野天神社（きたのてんじんしゃ）（北野） |date=2008-10-31 |publisher=Tokorozawa City Education Committee, Cultural Property Protection Division |accessdate=2015-06}} == {{nihongo|Worshipped deities|祭神|Saijin}} == * {{ill|Mononobe Tenjinsha|ja|物部天神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mononobe Tenjinsha|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (もののべてんじんじゃ): Enshrines {{ill|Nigihayahi|ja|ニギハヤヒ|lt=Kushitama Nigi Hayahito|lt_ja=饒速日命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nigihayahi|qq=}}, designated as the subsidiary shrine "Mononobe Tenjinsha" within the system; it is enshrined together with {{ill|Izumo Ihabishi Shrine|ja|出雲伊波比神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo Ihabishi Shrine|1=Izumoiwai Shrine, Moroyama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q30933323}}. * {{ill|Kuniichi Jigishinja|ja|国渭地祇神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuniichi Jigishinja|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 国渭地祇社|1=kuniichinoyashiro|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q55523456}} (くにいちぎじんじゃ): Enshrines {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en|Ōkuninushi|WD=Q276944|lt=Yachihoko no Mikoto}}, designated as the subsidiary shrine "Kuniichi Jigisha" ({{ill|Izumo Ihabishi Shrine|ja|出雲伊波比神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo Ihabishi Shrine|1=Izumoiwai Shrine, Moroyama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q30933323}} is enshrined together). * {{ill|Tenmantenjinja|ja|天満天神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmantenjinja|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (てんまんてんじんじゃ): Enshrines {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|1=Sugawara no Michizane|2=ja|3=菅原道真|ja|Sugawara no Michizane|1=Sugawara no Michizane|2=ja|3=菅原道真|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugawara no Michizane|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q382005}}. === 合祀 === * {{ill|Prince Munenaga|en|Prince Munenaga|WD=Q541057|lt=Souryo Prince}} (むねよししんのう) * {{ill|Kotesashi Myojin|ja|小手指明神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotesashi Myojin|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} * {{ill|Ame no Hohi|en|Ame no Hohi|WD=Q10940685|lt=Amenohohi no Mikoto}} * {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|en|Emperor Ōjin|WD=Q317997|lt=Emperor Ojin}} * {{ill|Yamato Takeru|en|Yamato Takeru|WD=Q461258|lt=Prince Yamato Takeru}} * {{ill|Ukanomitama|en|Ukanomitama|WD=Q3080728|lt=Ukano Mitama no Mikoto}} == History == According to shrine tradition, it is said that {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|日本武尊|1=Yamato Takeru|lt=Prince Yamato Takeru|3=ヤマトタケル|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Takeru|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Takeru|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ヤマトタケル|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q461258}} enshrined this site during his eastern expedition. In the {{ill|Edo period|en|Edo period|WD=Q184963|lt=Edo period}}, the Edo Bakufu granted {{ill|Shuinjo|ja|朱印状|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shuinjo|1=shuinjō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11093673}} to the shrine. * The Mononobe Tenjinsha was the tutelary shrine of the Mononobe clan (see {{ill|Mujashi Kunizukuri|ja|无邪志国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mujashi Kunizukuri|1=Musashi no Kuni no Miyatsuko|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11504612}} for the family) and continues to enshrine their ancestral deity, {{ill|Nigihayahi|ja|ニギハヤヒ|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nigihayahi|qq=}}. * As a Tenjin Shrine, it was first enshrined by {{ill|Sugawara no Shūsei|ja|菅原修成|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugawara no Shūsei|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, a 5th-generation descendant of {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|1=Sugawara no Michizane|2=ja|3=菅原道真|ja|Sugawara no Michizane|1=Sugawara no Michizane|2=ja|3=菅原道真|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugawara no Michizane|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q382005}}, in the first year of the {{ill|Chōtoku|en|Chōtoku|WD=Q1327213|lt=Chōtoku}} era (995) as a guardian in his capacity as {{ill|Musashi-no-Mori|ja|武蔵守|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Musashi-no-Mori|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 武蔵国司|1=musashikokushi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11546337}}, sent from Kyoto's {{ill|Kitano Tenmangū|en|Kitano Tenmangū|WD=Q662176|lt=Kitano Shrine}}. Subsequently, the shrine buildings were constructed under the auspices of figures such as {{ill|Minamoto no Yoshiie|en|Minamoto no Yoshiie|WD=Q32613|lt=Minamoto no Yoshiie}}, {{ill|Minamoto no Yoritomo|en|Minamoto no Yoritomo|WD=Q242800|lt=Minamoto no Yoritomo}}, {{ill|Ashikaga Takauji|en|Ashikaga Takauji|WD=Q297107|lt=Ashikaga Takauji}}, and {{ill|Maeda Toshiie|en|Maeda Toshiie|WD=Q1196817|lt=Maeda Toshiie}}. * Edo Shukkai-chō – From April 1 to 6 in the 7th year of the {{ill|Kyōhō|en|Kyōhō|WD=Q1145048|lt=Kyōhō}} era (1722), an opening ceremony ({{ill|Shukkai-chō|ja|出開帳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shukkai-chō|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 開帳|1=kaichō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q6347588}}) for the shrine's sacred object was held at the former {{ill|Mejiro Fudōin Hasedera|ja|目白不動院長谷寺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mejiro Fudōin Hasedera|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} in Edo, and on April 24 during that period, temple treasures such as hanging scrolls and documents were submitted to Edo Castle at the behest of the shogun.{{Cite web|和書|url=https://www.asahi-net.or.jp/~hm9k-ajm/musasinorekisi/gosikifudoutomusasino/mejirofudou/kitanotennjinndekaityou/kitanotennjinnsyadekaityou.htm |title=北野天神社江戸出開帳 |work=おたまじゃくし |date=2001-11-11 |publisher=Yasushima Kiichi|accessdate=2015-06}} == Shrine Grounds == Within the shrine precincts, a sanmichi (approach path) lined with {{ill|Torii|en|Torii|WD=Q234731|lt=torii}} and {{ill|stone lanterns|ja|石灯籠|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/stone lanterns|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 灯籠|1=Stone lantern|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q12012294}} is located on the west and south sides. The west side faces the old {{ill|Kamakura Kaidō|en|Kamakura Kaidō|WD=Q2389309|lt=Kamakura Kaidō}}, which runs north–south, and from the south side along {{ill|Saitama-Tokyo Road 179|ja|県道179号線|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saitama-Tokyo Road 179|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, multiple staircases and torii lead up to the haiden (worship hall). ; Shrines Within the Grounds * {{ill|Inari Shrine|ja|稲荷社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inari Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 稲荷神社|1=Inari shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q514480}} * {{ill|Yakumo Shrine|ja|八雲社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yakumo Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} * {{ill|Kōkūjinja (Tokorozawa)|ja|航空神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōkūjinja (Tokorozawa)|1=Aviation Shrines|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q30319396}} – Established on September 25, Showa 12 by {{ill|Yoshitoshi Tokugawa|en|Yoshitoshi Tokugawa|WD=Q5694703|lt=Tokugawa Yoshitoshi}}, at the {{ill|Tokorozawa Army Airfield|ja|所沢陸軍飛行場|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokorozawa Army Airfield|1=Tokorozawa Airfield|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11658682}}. Its establishment was inspired by the plight of aviation personnel who sacrificed their lives for the development of national aviation yet were not enshrined at {{ill|Yasukuni Shrine|en|Yasukuni Shrine|WD=Q242803|lt=Yasukuni Shrine}}; it was thus determined that a guardian deity for national aviation should be enshrined. In Showa 13, with the founding of the {{ill|Imperial Japanese Army Air Academy|en|Imperial Japanese Army Air Academy|WD=Q2822344|lt=Army Air Officer Academy}}, the shrine was relocated from Tokorozawa to Toyooka (present-day {{ill|Iruma Air Base|en|Iruma Air Base|WD=Q3015843|lt=Iruma Base}}). On September 3, Showa 20, before the academy site was seized by the U.S. military, the shrine was re-situated within its present grounds. * {{ill|Fumiko Tenjin Shrine|ja|文子天神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fumiko Tenjin Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|WD=Q135579708}} – Enshrines Fumiko, who served as the wet nurse ({{ill|Wet nurse|en|Wet nurse|WD=Q472898|lt=wet nurse}}) of {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|1=Sugawara no Michizane|2=ja|3=菅原道真|ja|Sugawara no Michizane|1=Sugawara no Michizane|2=ja|3=菅原道真|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugawara no Michizane|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q382005}}, known as {{ill|Tajihi Fumiko|ja|多治比文子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tajihi Fumiko|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. * {{ill|Kotesashi Jinja|ja|小手指神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotesashi Jinja|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|WD=Q135579709}} – Enshrines the war dead (heroic spirits) of the Kotesashi area. ; Trees on the Grounds * {{ill|Mikotozakura|ja|尊桜|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mikotozakura|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} – A cherry tree said to have been planted in front of the shrine by {{ill|Yamato Takeru|en|Yamato Takeru|WD=Q461258|lt=Yamato Takeru}}, which repeatedly dies and regrows (exhibiting {{ill|Noda|ja|蘖（ひこばえ）|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Noda|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}). * {{ill|Dainagon Ume|ja|大納言梅|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dainagon Ume|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} – Planted in the 18th year of the {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|en|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|WD=Q1145058|lt=Tenshō Era}} (1590) by {{ill|Maeda Toshiie|en|Maeda Toshiie|WD=Q1196817|lt=Maeda Toshiie}}, currently the second generation as of 2015. It is said that Maeda Toshiie, who claimed descent from {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|1=Sugawara no Michizane|2=ja|3=菅原道真|ja|Sugawara no Michizane|1=Sugawara no Michizane|2=ja|3=菅原道真|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugawara no Michizane|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q382005}} and used the Ume crest ({{ill|Ume Crest|ja|梅紋|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ume Crest|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ウメ|1=Prunus mume|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q157763}}), revived the shrine by planting a single plum tree during the 【ill|Odawara Campaign|ja|小田原攻め】; his title at that time was {{ill|Dainagon|en|Dainagon|WD=Q1354706|lt=Dainagon}}. ; Other Elements Within the Grounds * A stone monument recording the origin of the local name "Kitano" – Established on September 25, {{ill|Heisei era|en|Heisei era|WD=Q234510|lt=Heisei}} 18 (2006). Although recent land reorganization has changed the shrine's address to Kotesashi Motomachi, the surrounding area retains the name "Kitano" as derived from this shrine. * The camp site of {{ill|Prince Munenaga|en|Prince Munenaga|WD=Q541057|lt=Souryo Prince}}. * A temizuya (water ablution pavilion) – Recently (in the 2010s) rebuilt with a ceiling mural depicting a {{ill|dragon|ja|龍|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/dragon|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 竜|1=dragon|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q7559}}. * A kaguraden (dancing hall). * A stone marker. * The sacred horse ({{ill|Shinme|ja|神馬|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinme|qq=}}). Suwa Jinja Kotesashi.jpg|Suwa Shrine == List of Festivals == * New Year Festival (元旦祭, January 1) – Ritual talismans ("祈祷札") are distributed. * Hatsumōde (初詣) (January 1) * Setsubun Festival (節分祭, February 3) – Corresponds to the Ōharae at Kitano Tenjin Shrine; the "Shikinaisha Kitano Shrine Ōharae Shinpū" is distributed. * Hatsu-uma Festival (初午祭, February 11) – Held at the Inari Shrine within the precincts; "Inari Shrine Shinpū" is distributed. * Kinen-sai (祈年祭, February 27) – Also known as "Toshigoi no Matsuri"; "Kinen-sai Shinpū" is distributed. * Spring Seasonal Festival (春季例大祭, March 21) – Paired with the autumn festival, this is the most important festival at the shrine; "Kuniichi Jigisha Kaiun Shugoshinpū" is distributed. * Spring Festival (春祭, March 25) – Also called "Nibanmachi"; "Mononobe Tenjinsha Shinpū" is distributed. * Sericulture Festival (養蚕祭, April 3) – Held at the Bunkoten Shrine within the precincts; "Bunkoten Shrine Shinpū" is distributed. * Memorial Festival (慰霊祭, April 15) – Held at the Kotesashi Jinja to commemorate war dead from the Nisshin and Nichiro periods. * Yakumo Festival (八雲祭) – Held on the evening of July 14 and main festival on July 15; "Yakumo Shrine Prayer Talisman for Disaster Exorcism" is distributed. * Autumn Seasonal Festival (秋季例大祭, Late September) – Annual musical offerings and a village kagura are performed biennially. * Niiname-sai (新嘗祭, November 23) – "Niiname-sai Shinpū" is distributed.{{Cite web|和書|url=https://kitanotenjin.com/nenkangyouji.html |title=北野天神社のお祭り |publisher=Kitano Tenjin Shrine |accessdate=2022-01-15}} == Footnotes == {{reflist}} == References == * Tokorozawa City Historical Research No.3 [https://www.city.tokorozawa.saitama.jp/iitokoro/enjoy/rekishi/sisi02.html About the Kitano Tenjin Shrine Engi Picture] (Author: Nakahara Nakatomo) == Further Reading == * {{cite book|和書|title=[[Shinpen Musashi Fudoki-kō]]|volume=巻ノ158 入間郡ノ3|chapter=Kitano-mura Tenjinsha|id={{NDLJP|764001/72}}|publisher=Geography Bureau, Ministry of Home Affairs|date=1884-6}} == External Links == {{commonscat|Kitano-Tenjin-sha, Tokorozawa}} * [https://kitanotenjin.com/] (Official shrine website) * {{Cite web|和書|title=Mononobe Tenjinsha, Kuniichi Jigishinja, Tenmantenjinja (Kitano Tenjin Shrine)|url=https://www.saitama-jinjacho.or.jp/shrine/8910/ |publisher=Saitama Prefectural Shrine Agency|accessdate=2018-03-12}} * {{Cite web|和書|title=Kitano Tenjin Shrine (きたのてんじんじゃ)|url=https://www.city.tokorozawa.saitama.jp/iitokoro/enjoy/kids/shokai/meisyokyuseki/kitanotenjinsya.html |publisher=Tokorozawa City|date=2008-10-31|accessdate=2017-10-15}} {{translated page|ja|北野天神社 (所沢市)|version=101465493|comment=Imported full ja history}} [[ceb:Kitano Tenjinsha (Tokorozawa)]] [[ja:北野天神社]] {{Commons category|Kitano-Tenjin-sha, Tokorozawa}} [[ja:北野天神社 (所沢市)]] {{Shinja |名称 = {{ill|Mononobe Tenjin Shrine|ja|物部天神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mononobe Tenjin Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}・{{ill|Kuniichi Jigishinja|ja|国渭地祇神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuniichi Jigishinja|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 国渭地祇社|1=kuniichinoyashiro|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q55523456}}

tradition, it is said that {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|日本武尊|1=Yamato Takeru|lt=Prince Yamato Takeru|3=ヤマトタケル|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Takeru|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Takeru|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ヤマトタケル|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q461258}} enshrined this site during his eastern expedition. In the Edo period, the Edo Bakufu granted {{ill|Shuinjo|ja|朱印状|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shuinjo|1=shuinjō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11093673}} to the shrine. * The Mononobe Tenjin Shrine served as the tutelary shrine of the Mononobe clan (see {{ill|Mujashi Kunizukuri|ja|无邪志国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mujashi Kunizukuri|1=Musashi no Kuni no Miyatsuko|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11504612}} for details on the clan) and still enshrines their ancestral deity, {{ill|Nigihayahi|ja|ニギハヤヒ|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nigihayahi|qq=}}. * As a Tenjin shrine, it was established in the first year of the {{ill|Chōtoku|en|Chōtoku|WD=Q1327213|lt=Chōtoku}} era (995) when {{ill|Sugawara no Shūsei|ja|菅原修成|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugawara no Shūsei|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, a fifth-generation descendant of {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|1=Sugawara no Michizane|2=ja|3=菅原道真|ja|Sugawara no Michizane|1=Sugawara no Michizane|2=ja|3=菅原道真|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugawara no Michizane|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q382005}}, was commissioned as {{ill|Musashi-no-Mori|ja|武蔵守|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Musashi-no-Mori|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 武蔵国司|1=musashikokushi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11546337}} from Kyoto’s {{ill|Kitano Tenmangū|en|Kitano Tenmangū|WD=Q662176|lt=Kitano Tenmangu}}; thereafter, the shrine buildings were constructed under the auspices of figures such as {{ill|Minamoto no Yoshiie|en|Minamoto no Yoshiie|WD=Q32613|lt=Minamoto no Yoshiie}}, {{ill|Minamoto no Yoritomo|en|Minamoto no Yoritomo|WD=Q242800|lt=Minamoto no Yoritomo}}, {{ill|Ashikaga Takauji|en|Ashikaga Takauji|WD=Q297107|lt=Ashikaga Takauji}}, and {{ill|Maeda Toshiie|en|Maeda Toshiie|WD=Q1196817|lt=Maeda Toshiie}}. * Edo Shukkai-chō – From April 1 to 6 in the 7th year of the {{ill|Kyōhō|en|Kyōhō|WD=Q1145048|lt=Kyōhō}} era (1722), an opening ceremony for the shrine’s sacred object was held at the former {{ill|Mejiro Fudōin Hasedera|ja|目白不動院長谷寺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mejiro Fudōin Hasedera|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} in Edo, and on April 24 during that period, shrine treasures such as hanging scrolls and documents were submitted to Edo Castle at the shogun’s behest.{{Cite web|和書|url=https://www.asahi-net.or.jp/~hm9k-ajm/musasinorekisi/gosikifudoutomusasino/mejirofudou/kitanotennjinndekaityou/kitanotennjinnsyadekaityou.htm |title=北野天神社江戸出開帳 |work=おたまじゃくし |date=2001-11-11 |publisher=Yasushima Kiichi|accessdate=2015-06}} == Shrine Grounds == The shrine grounds feature an approach path lined with {{ill|Torii|en|Torii|WD=Q234731|lt=torii}} and {{ill|stone lanterns|ja|石灯籠|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/stone lanterns|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 灯籠|1=Stone lantern|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q12012294}} on the west and south sides. The west side faces the old {{ill|Kamakura Kaidō|en|Kamakura Kaidō|WD=Q2389309|lt=Kamakura Kaidō}}, which runs north–south, and from the south side along {{ill|Saitama-Tokyo Road 179|ja|県道179号線|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saitama-Tokyo Road 179|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, multiple staircases and torii lead up to the area in front of the haiden (worship hall). ; Shrines Within the Grounds * {{ill|Inari Shrine|ja|稲荷社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inari Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 稲荷神社|1=Inari shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q514480}} * {{ill|Yakumo Shrine|ja|八雲社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yakumo Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} * {{ill|Kōkūjinja (Tokorozawa)|ja|航空神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōkūjinja (Tokorozawa)|1=Aviation Shrines|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q30319396}} – Established on September 25, Showa 12 by {{ill|Yoshitoshi Tokugawa|en|Yoshitoshi Tokugawa|WD=Q5694703|lt=Tokugawa Yoshitoshi}} at the {{ill|Tokorozawa Army Airfield|ja|所沢陸軍飛行場|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokorozawa Army Airfield|1=Tokorozawa Airfield|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11658682}}. Its establishment was prompted by the plight of aviation personnel who sacrificed their lives for the development of national aviation yet were not enshrined at {{ill|Yasukuni Shrine|en|Yasukuni Shrine|WD=Q242803|lt=Yasukuni Shrine}}. In Showa 13, with the founding of the {{ill|Imperial Japanese Army Air Academy|en|Imperial Japanese Army Air Academy|WD=Q2822344|lt=Army Air Officer Academy}}, the shrine was relocated from Tokorozawa to Toyooka (present-day {{ill|Iruma Air Base|en|Iruma Air Base|WD=Q3015843|lt=Iruma Base}}). On September 3, Showa 20, before the academy site was seized by the U.S. military, the shrine was re-situated within its current grounds. * {{ill|Fumiko Tenjin Shrine|ja|文子天神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fumiko Tenjin Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|WD=Q135579708}} – Enshrines Fumiko, who served as the wet nurse ({{ill|Wet nurse|en|Wet nurse|WD=Q472898|lt=wet nurse}}) of {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|1=Sugawara no Michizane|2=ja|3=菅原道真|ja|Sugawara no Michizane|1=Sugawara no Michizane|2=ja|3=菅原道真|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugawara no Michizane|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q382005}}, known as {{ill|Tajihi Fumiko|ja|多治比文子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tajihi Fumiko|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. * {{ill|Kotesashi Jinja|ja|小手指神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotesashi Jinja|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|WD=Q135579709}} – Enshrines the war dead (heroic spirits) of the Kotesashi area. Kitano Tenjin Inari.jpg|Inari Shrine Kitano Tenjin Yagumo.jpg|Yakumo Shrine KitanoTenjin AyakoJinja.jpg|Fumiko Tenjin Shrine Kotesashi-jinja 14.jpg|Kotesashi Jinja and Kōkūjinja ; Trees on the Grounds * {{ill|Mikoto-zakura|ja|尊桜|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mikoto-zakura|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} – A cherry tree said to have been planted in front of the shrine by {{ill|Yamato Takeru|en|Yamato Takeru|WD=Q461258|lt=Yamato Takeru}}, which repeatedly dies and regrows (exhibiting {{ill|nodate|ja|蘖（ひこばえ）|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/nodate|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}). * {{ill|Dainagon Ume|ja|大納言梅|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dainagon Ume|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} – Planted in the 18th year of the {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|en|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|WD=Q1145058|lt=Tenshō Era}} (1590) by {{ill|Maeda Toshiie|en|Maeda Toshiie|WD=Q1196817|lt=Maeda Toshiie}}, currently in its second generation as of 2015. It is named after Maeda Toshiie’s former Rank, {{ill|Dainagon|en|Dainagon|WD=Q1354706|lt=Dainagon}}, commemorating his restoration of the shrine during the {{ill|Siege of Odawara|en|Siege of Odawara|WD=Q4372123|lt=Odawara Campaign}}. ; Other Elements Within the Grounds * A stone monument recording the origin of the local name “Kitano” – Established on September 25, {{ill|Heisei era|en|Heisei era|WD=Q234510|lt=Heisei}} 18 (2006); it states that the surrounding area “Kitano” derives its name from this shrine. * The campsite of {{ill|Prince Munenaga|en|Prince Munenaga|WD=Q541057|lt=Souryo Prince}}. * A temizuya (water ablution pavilion) – Recently rebuilt (in the 2010s) with a ceiling mural depicting a {{ill|dragon|ja|龍|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/dragon|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 竜|1=dragon|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q7559}}. * A kaguraden (dancing hall). * A power stone. * A divine horse ({{ill|Shinme|ja|神馬|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinme|qq=}}). Dainagon-ume Kitano-Tenjin-sha.jpg|Dainagon Ume Kitano Tenjin shinme.jpg|Sacred Horse == Cultural Properties == === Saitama Prefecture-designated Cultural Properties === * Tangible Cultural Property: ** Kitano Tenjin Shrine Engi (Origin Legend) (paintings) – Consisting of 7 silk-colored hanging scrolls and 7 old logs.{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.city.tokorozawa.saitama.jp/iitokoro/enjoy/bunkakyoyo/bunkazai/kenshiteibunkazai/bunzai_20100510170056823.html |title=Kitano Tenjin Shrine Engi, with 7 old logs |publisher=Tokorozawa City Education Committee, Cultural Property Protection Division |accessdate=2015-06}} === Tokorozawa City-designated Cultural Properties === * Tangible Cultural Property: ** The Ume Song Monument of Kitano Tenjin Shrine (a scenic spot) – Established in the 2nd year of the {{ill|Kyōwa|en|Kyōwa|WD=Q960763|lt=Kyōwa Era}} (1802); it is the oldest song monument in the city.{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.city.tokorozawa.saitama.jp/iitokoro/enjoy/bunkakyoyo/bunkazai/shishiteibunkazai/meisyo/bunzai_20100601150043467.html |title=尊桜の歌碑 |publisher=Tokorozawa City Education Committee, Cultural Property Protection Division |accessdate=2015-06}} ** Medieval Documents of Kitano Tenjin Shrine – A collection of 11 documents including a donation letter from the Ashikaga clan.{{Cite web|和書|url=https://www.city.tokorozawa.saitama.jp/iitokoro/enjoy/bunkakyoyo/bunkazai/shishiteibunkazai/komonjo/bunzai_20100810104554996.html |title=Kitano Tenjin Shrine Medieval Documents |publisher=Tokorozawa City Education Committee, Cultural Property Protection Division |accessdate=2015-06}} == Concurrent Shrines == * {{ill|Fujimori Inari Shrine (Tokorozawa)|ja|藤森稲荷神社 (所沢市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujimori Inari Shrine (Tokorozawa)|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|WD=Q135579710}} * {{ill|Rokusho Shrine (Tokorozawa)|ja|六所神社 (所沢市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rokusho Shrine (Tokorozawa)|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 上新井|1=Kamiarai|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11359054}} * {{ill|Suwa Shrine (Tokorozawa)|ja|諏訪神社 (所沢市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suwa Shrine (Tokorozawa)|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} – Located at 1-17-21 Kotesashi. Suwa Jinja Kotesashi.jpg|Suwa Shrine == List of Festivals == * New Year Festival (元旦祭, January 1) – "Prayer talismans" ("祈祷札") are distributed. * Hatsumōde (初詣) (January 1) * Setsubun Festival (節分祭, February 3) – Corresponds to the Ōharae at Kitano Tenjin Shrine; the "Shikinaisha Kitano Shrine Ōharae Shinpū" is distributed. * Hatsu-uma Festival (初午祭, February 11) – Held at the Inari Shrine within the precincts; "Inari Shrine Shinpū" is distributed. * Kinen-sai (祈年祭, February 27) – Also known as "Toshigoi no Matsuri"; "Kinen-sai Shinpū" is distributed. * Spring Seasonal Festival (春季例大祭, March 21) – Paired with the autumn festival, this is the most important festival at the shrine; "Kuniichi Jigisha Kaiun Shugoshinpū" is distributed. * Spring Festival (春祭, March 25) – Also called "Nibanmachi"; "Mononobe Tenjinsha Shinpū" is distributed. * Sericulture Festival (養蚕祭, April 3) – Held at the Bunkoten Shrine within the precincts; "Bunkoten Shrine Shinpū" is distributed. * Memorial Festival (慰霊祭, April 15) – Held at Kotesashi Jinja to commemorate war dead from the Nisshin and Nichiro periods. * Yakumo Festival (八雲祭) – Held on the evening of July 14 (yo-miya) and the main festival on July 15; "Yakumo Shrine Prayer Talisman for Disaster Exorcism" is distributed. * Autumn Seasonal Festival (秋季例大祭, Late September) – Musical offerings are made annually, and a village kagura is performed every two years. * Niiname-sai (新嘗祭, November 23) – "Niiname-sai Shinpū" is distributed.{{Cite web|和書|url=https://kitanotenjin.com/nenkangyouji.html |title=Kitano Tenjin Shrine Festival|publisher=Kitano Tenjin Shrine |accessdate=2022-01-15}} == Footnotes == {{reflist}} == References == * Tokorozawa City Historical Research No.3 [https://www.city.tokorozawa.saitama.jp/iitokoro/enjoy/rekishi/sisi02.html About the Kitano Tenjin Shrine Engi Picture] (Author: Nakahara Nakatomo) == Further Reading == * {{cite
